articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Littler in shock first-round exit as defending champion loses to Luke Woodhouse
articles.summary: World No 1 Luke Littler suffers shock 2-1 defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night in Leicester as six-time champion Michael van Gerwen is also eliminated; watch day two of the World Grand Prix live on Sky Sports+ from 6pm, Tuesday
articles.body:
Littler won the first set, but was far from his best as Woodhouse spurned several chances at double to have taken the opener into a deciding leg.

Woodhouse made no mistake in sets two and three, however, to see him pull off one of the biggest upsets in the hostory of the double-in, double-out tournament.

He'll face former finalist Nathan Aspinall in the second round after he overcame Kevin Doets in a final-leg decider earlier on the opening night.

Following his stunning early exit, Little posted on his Instagram: "Well played @lukewoodly180 was a good game, good one to be apart of aswell.

"Both hit, both missed but Luke took his chance and nice week off now, all the best to Luke for rest of tournament."

Littler followed that up by signalling his intent to now attend the Super League Grand Final on Saturday, which features his beloved Warrington Wolves - and would have clashed with the Grand Prix semi-finals.

"May aswell get myself to OT (Old Trafford) now I'm out. LETS GO THE WIRE @warringtonrlfc," Littler added.

Following his seismic victory over Littler, Woodhouse said afterwards: "Luke's not a robot. He's going to have days and weeks and whatever where he's not right on it.

"But look I think people have echoed it and I'm going to say it again, he's one of a kind Luke.

"I hope people will take the time to appreciate how good he is and not give him a hard time. You might not see another Luke Littler ever again."

Van Gerwen dumped out but Price, Clayton win

Elsewhere, not only were Van Gerwen's hopes of a seventh Grand Prix crown dashed but he suffered a third-straight first-round loss in the tournament as Ryan Joyce came back from a set down to defeat the Dutchman.

Welsh duo Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton , winners of the Grand Prix in 2020 and 2021 respectively, also progressed, with Price putting in the performance of the night as he averaged 101.61 and dropped only one leg in beating Sebastian Bialecki.

Clayton was made to work much harder by Krzysztof Ratajski, one of six matches (out of eight) to go the distance on the opening night.

Cameron Menzies and Kevin Doets both missed match darts when losing out to Ross Smith and Aspinall , respectively.

Each had chances to wrap up two-set victories, but Menzies missed two looks at tops before Smith swept him aside 3-0 in the deciding set, while Doets spurned three match darts - including a wild miss at bullseye - and Aspinall would ultimately take it in a last-leg decider in the third set.

Danny Noppert came flying out of the blocks to open the night, claiming five consecutive legs before Niko Springer, out of nowhere, claimed the next three to take the second set, before normal service resumed in the third.

Wessel Nijman , meanwhile, rounded off the evening with a routine 2-0 victory over Rob Cross.

He'll face Clayton next, while Noppert takes on MVG conqueror Joyce and Price goes up against Smith, who revealed he almost pulled out of the World Grand Prix after being hospitalised in the week leading up to the tournament.

"I've had a week from hell," Smith said after his first-round victory. "I've come home and picked up some sort of virus and I've had a few issues with my heart as well.

"I was in hospital on Friday. I thought I was pulling out of this event on Saturday, so to be here is an achievement in itself. Let alone play and win like that, I'm very happy."

The second round takes place across Wednesday and Thursday, with the quarter-finals on Friday, semi-finals on Saturday and final on Sunday.

articles.title: Kirill Marchenko Traded to Maple Leafs, New Contract Details and Blue Jackets' Return Revealed
articles.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs are adding some offensive firepower to their roster ahead of the 2026-27 NHL season with the addition of right-winger Kirill Marchenko.
articles.body:
The Toronto Maple Leafs are adding some offensive firepower to their roster ahead of the 2026-27 NHL season with the addition of right-winger Kirill Marchenko.

After NHL insider Elliotte Friedman reported Monday the Maple Leafs were in "deep" trade talks for the Columbus Blue Jackets right-winger, Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic reported the deal was happening and also involved Matthew Knies:

Friedman reported on the additional players and noted Toronto will also extend Marchenko with a new deal:

The trade was the conclusion of an ongoing process on Monday:

This comes after Columbus and Marchenko were unable to come to terms on a contract extension. He was also rather noncommittal about his status with the franchise when asked about his future in Columbus earlier this offseason:

Marchenko was scheduled for restricted free agency after the upcoming season, so there was likely motivation on Columbus' part to trade him if he had no interest in returning on an extension.

It at least gets something in return with this move for someone who didn't seem to have a shortage of suitors, as Friedman recently reported on his 32 Thoughts podcast (h/t Nick Goss of NBC Sports Boston).

"Montreal, everybody knows about, the Islanders I mentioned a couple pods ago," Friedman said. "Toronto I think has really tried to keep their interest secret, but it's kind of seeped out. I think Winnipeg at one point kind of looked into it.

"I heard Boston made an offer at one point. I had some people say Vegas, I had some other people say they weren't sure it was Vegas. I have to think Seattle is around this. They've really been looking at trying to grab a top-end player and they could make this deal."

So much interest, including from his eventual destination in Toronto, wasn't particularly surprising, as Marchenko is 26 years old and coming off back-to-back impressive seasons. He scored 74 points on 43 assists and 31 goals in 2024-25 and then followed up with 67 points on 40 assists and 27 goals in 2025-26.

Given his age and the reality he was playing for a Blue Jackets team that missed the playoffs both seasons, it is reasonable to expect him to be even more productive in the future if he is surrounded by more talent in Toronto.

The Maple Leafs are certainly looking to return to the postseason after missing out last year.

They snapped a streak of nine straight seasons making the playoffs in part because of a middling offense that was 16th in the league in goals per game. Adding someone like Marchenko could help improve those numbers and perhaps lead to a return to the postseason.

As for the Blue Jackets, they will continue to rebuild with the addition of the 23-year-old Knies. The forward tallied 66 points on 43 assists and 23 goals last season.

articles.title: Kevin McGonigle Was Confused by His Curtain Call
articles.summary: Kevin McGonigle got a curtain call in the Tigers finale and had no idea it was coming. #Tigers
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers were trailing 4-0 in the bottom of the seventh inning against the Pittsburgh Pirates in the final game of the 2026 MLB season on Sunday. Kevin McGonigle hit a solo home run to left-center, and it turned out to be his last at-bat of the year.

In the top of the eighth inning, manager A.J. Hinch pulled McGonigle after the rookie had already taken the field at third base. McGonigle pointed to himself and asked, "Me?" Then came the standing ovation from the Comerica Park crowd. The 22-year-old played 156 games for Detroit in 2026 and was one of the few bright spots in a 76-86 season.

Kevin McGonigle Speaks Out About Being Pulled

McGonigle talked to Jason Beck of MLB.com after the game about the eighth-inning move. "I was more confused. I didn't expect that. It was really cool," he said.

A Rookie Season Among the Best Since 1947

McGonigle finished with a .278 batting average, 18 home runs and 72 RBIs, plus 12 stolen bases in 16 attempts. He posted a .376 on-base percentage, a .430 slugging percentage and an .806 OPS. He entered Sunday leading all American League position players in bWAR , not just rookies, and his 6.9 mark would be the eighth highest by a rookie since the Rookie of the Year Award debuted in 1947. He could well win the American League award this year.

A.J. Hinch Was Going to Pull Him in the Seventh Inning

Hinch had planned to take McGonigle out after his seventh-inning at-bat and had a pinch-runner ready to go. The home run foiled that. Hinch told Beck:

"I think we found the one thing we get to talk to Kevin about improving over the winter, which is the curtain call." "I thought he was going to single or walk or double or something. And then he goes ahead and hits a homer." "Respecting what that accomplishment is matters to me. So I wanted to at least get him a chance to get an ovation in front of our home fans. I probably should've gone to the mound and actually told him what I was doing, but it gave the boys on the bench some ammo to get under Kevin's skin."

"I thought he was going to single or walk or double or something. And then he goes ahead and hits a homer."

"Respecting what that accomplishment is matters to me. So I wanted to at least get him a chance to get an ovation in front of our home fans. I probably should've gone to the mound and actually told him what I was doing, but it gave the boys on the bench some ammo to get under Kevin's skin."

Hinch also called it an "incredible season, and a fitting way for him to cap it with some good at-bats today and the opposite-field homer." The Tigers missed the postseason, but McGonigle gave them plenty to build on heading into 2027.

articles.title: How the mighty have fallen: Steph Curry reacts to Warriors expectations
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry is back healthy. He was shocked to hear expectations placed on the Warriors.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO ― The Golden State Warriors will only go as far as their franchise leader Stephen Curry will take them.

That is partially why it was important for him to ink a deal to return to the Warriors for the next year or two. Now that the dust has settled and the ink is dry, an area of focus for Curry will be his availability.

Curry missed 39 games for the Warriors last year with knee issues. Entering his 18th season, he's not getting any younger. He spent the offseason nursing his knee through many rounds of golf during the summer, now he's ready for basketball.

"Knee is feeling great, ready to go. No issues at all. There is a management element of it for sure where you just have to be mindful of everything that you're doing in practice, games, preparation," Curry said. "We haven't talked about the game schedule yet or anything like that where I'm kind of getting too far ahead of myself, but for training camp and the preseason schedule and getting myself into shape and ready to go, there's no limitations at all."

Curry is more confident going into the year, he said, after becoming stronger and understanding that he doesn't have 18-year-old knees anymore, let alone 28-year-old ligaments.

"So I'm excited to get out there and hoop. I feel like I've built a really good foundation over the summer to be in a much better position up until, what, November last year, it wasn't really any kind of signs or symptoms, but I feel a lot stronger and more understanding of what I'm dealing with," he said. "That gives me a lot of confidence going into the year."

articles.title: White Sox Wild Card Series: Watch Schedule And TV Details
articles.summary: Chicago White Sox fans can watch the Wild Card Series against Houston on NBCSN and Peacock. Get the full schedule, times, and broadcast info here.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox have punched their ticket to the postseason, but the path to glory starts with a tricky viewing puzzle. The team faces the Houston Astros in a best-of-three Wild Card Series that kicks off on Tuesday, September 29. All games will take place at Daikin Park in Houston, meaning the White Sox must win on the road to advance. Fans across the country need to know exactly where to look to catch the action, as the broadcast setup is more complex than a standard regular-season game.

Most fans will need a streaming subscription to watch the White Sox play. NBCSN will broadcast the initial two contests while Peacock offers live streaming, as reported by Yahoo Sports . NBCSN is a cable channel that does not have widespread carriage anymore, so many viewers will miss the game on their standard TV packages. Per South Side Sox , the only local option for color commentary is Steve Stone, who will join the Peacock broadcast to provide analysis. This means a Peacock subscription is the most reliable way for fans to follow the team, with plans starting at $12.99 a month.

The schedule is tight and follows a specific pattern for all four Wild Card matchups. Game 1 is set for 4 p.m. CT on Tuesday, followed by Game 2 at the same time on Wednesday. If the series goes to a deciding third game, it will happen on Thursday, October 1. The start time for Game 3 depends on when the other series conclude, per the schedule released by NBC Sports . Fans must check their streaming apps or cable guides closely, as the time could shift to 1 p.m. or 7 p.m. CT based on the results of the Phillies , Cubs , and Red Sox games.

NBC has brought in a strong team to call the action for this series. The broadcast features play-by-play announcer Tom McCarthy, who is known for calling Philadelphia Phillies games. Geoff Blum and Steve Stone, representing the Astros and White Sox respectively, will accompany him as analysts. Per NBC Sports, former pitcher Adam Ottavino will serve as the "Inside the Pitch" analyst, while field reporter Britney Eurton will provide updates from the dugout. This setup ensures fans get deep insights from former players who know the teams well.

There is a catch for those who prefer traditional cable over streaming. NBCSN returned in late 2025 but is only carried on a few services like Xfinity, YouTube TV, and Fubo, according to Yahoo Sports. If a fan does not have one of these specific providers, they cannot watch on TV and must use Peacock. This split in the broadcast rights means some fans might be left out if they do not have the right subscription. The network is trying to balance its cable and streaming platforms, but it creates a hurdle for the average viewer trying to tune in.

Playing the entire series in Houston is a significant disadvantage for the White Sox. Per South Side Sox, the compressed playoff schedule leaves no room for a travel day, forcing the lower seed to play all three potential games in the opponent's stadium. This setup tests the team's mental toughness and ability to perform under pressure without home-field support.

The stakes are high for a team that has struggled to find consistency in recent years. Every pitch matters when the series is short and played entirely on the road. If the White Sox can overcome the odds and the difficult viewing setup for fans, they could advance to the Division Series. The Division Series begins on Saturday, October 3, giving the team very little time to rest or prepare if they win. The path to the World Series starts here in Houston, and the fans watching from home will need to be ready for a grueling battle.

articles.title: Olise scores late to grab France 1-0 Nations League win at Belgium
articles.summary: Bayern Munich star Olise set off from inside his own half to score the winner in the 88th minute.
articles.body:
Michael Olise’s magnificent late strike gave France a 1-0 victory in Belgium in the UEFA Nations League as Zinedine Zidane made it two wins out of two since being named coach.

Bayern Munich star Olise, who was one of the outstanding players at the World Cup where France reached the semifinals, came off the bench late on with the game in Brussels on Monday goalless, and set off from inside his own half to score the winner in the 88th minute.

The win follows a 1-0 success away to Turkiye last Friday in Zidane’s first game at the helm after succeeding Didier Deschamps as France coach following the World Cup.

France are therefore top of Nations League Group A1 with six points, three points ahead of Belgium and Italy, with the latter winning 4-1 in Turkiye on Monday.

Les Bleus play host to Italy next at the Stade de France on Friday in what will be Zidane’s homecoming. France will then entertain Belgium on October 5.

Zidane was without captain Kylian Mbappe, with the Real Madrid striker having returned to his club for treatment after injuring his left knee while scoring the winner against Turkiye.

The French lineup at the King Baudouin Stadium showed nine changes, with goalkeeper Mike Maignan and Chelsea defender Maxence Lacroix the only players to keep their places.

There was notably a debut in midfield for Lucas Da Cunha of Como in Italy, as well as in attack for Esteban Lepaul of Rennes, the top scorer in France’s Ligue 1 last season.

Belgium, in contrast, made only two changes to the team that started during Friday’s 2-0 win in Italy for what was new coach Mark van Bommel’s home bow.

France had the better of the chances with Paris Saint-Germain’s Desire Doue cracking a shot off the bar in the first half and Da Cunha striking the post early in the second half.

But the contest was heading to an unremarkable goalless conclusion until Olise intervened, having been sent on in the 77th minute in place of Liverpool winger Bradley Barcola.

The London-born player collected possession inside his own half and advanced all the way to the edge of the Belgian box before curling a shot beyond the reach of Senne Lammens into the bottom-left corner of the net.

articles.title: Maple Leafs Acquire Marchenko From Blue Jackets, Sign Six-Year Extension In Blockbuster Trade
articles.summary: With the NHL regular season on the horizon, the Toronto Maple Leafs and Columbus Blue Jackets have agreed to a huge trade involving Kirill Marchenko and Matt...
articles.body:
The Toronto Maple Leafs have made one last splash before the start of the season.

Columbus Blue Jackets forwards Kirill Marchenko , Miles Wood and goaltender Elvis Merzlikins have been traded to the Maple Leafs in exchange for Matthew Knies , Steven Lorentz , Emil Andrae and a conditional 2027 second-round pick.

In addition, the 26-year-old has agreed to a six-year, $75-million extension that will keep him under contract in Toronto until the conclusion of the 2032-33 season.

This news comes after months of speculation on the Russian winger's future with the franchise, with rumors suggesting he was not open to signing an extension in Columbus when his three-year, $11.5-million contract expired at the end of this upcoming season.

Marchenko was a second-round pick of the Blue Jackets in the 2018 NHL Draft and made his debut in the 2022-23 season, recording 25 points in 59 games, with 21 of them being goals.

He has put together 208 points in 292 games across his four seasons with the franchise and has led the team in goals in the last three, with his best year coming in 2024-25 where he scored 31 goals and finished with 74 points in 79 games.

Merzlikins will join Marchenko in Toronto but is out indefinitely after undergoing shoulder surgery during the off-season . The 32-year-old has played 124 games over the last three seasons with the Blue Jackets and has put together an .890 save percentage and a 3.34 goals-against average.

The Latvian netminder is entering the final season of a five-year deal that carries a $5.4 million AAV.

Wood is set to enter his 10th NHL season and will be joining his fourth team with the Maple Leafs. The 31-year-old suited up for 54 games with the Blue Jackets last season, scoring eight goals and finishing with 14 points.

Heading the other way to Columbus, Knies was a second-round pick of the Maple Leafs in the 2021 NHL Draft and made his debut towards the end of the 2022-23 season. The 23-year-old is coming off a 23-goal, 66-point campaign and has put together 160 points in 240 career games with Toronto.

"Matthew is a big, strong power forward who combines tough, hard-nosed physical play with outstanding offensive skills, Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell said in a statement released by the team . "He is a young player with great character and work ethic and we couldn't be more excited to welcome him to the Blue Jackets family."

Knies is set to enter the second season of a six-year, $46.5-million extension ($7.75 million AAV) that will keep him under contract with the Blue Jackets until 2031.

Lorentz spent the past two seasons with the Maple Leafs and previously won a Stanley Cup with the Florida Panthers in the 2023-24 season. Andrae was acquired by the Maple Leafs in a trade earlier in the off-season that sent goaltender Joseph Woll to the Philadelphia Flyers .

articles.title: NHL Trade Grades: Blue Jackets Send Kirill Marchenko to Maple Leafs for Matthew Knies
articles.summary: If there was any doubt the NHL is in a new era, this may be the final blow. The end of preseason can be a manic period for end-of-the-roster maneuvering, but teams typically either get the big stuff done during the summer or wait until they settle into a new season.
articles.body:
If there was any doubt the NHL is in a new era, this may be the final blow. The end of preseason can be a manic period for end-of-the-roster maneuvering, but teams typically either get the big stuff done during the summer or wait until they settle into a new season.

With a growing salary cap, front offices willing to stray from tradition, and the peak of a player empowerment movement, the ground was set for a blockbuster like this. The Maple Leafs and Blue Jackets are swapping prominent young wingers. Kirill Marchenko gets the move out of Columbus that he sought, while Matthew Knies departs Toronto.

How does this change the outlook for both teams, both this season and beyond? Let's analyze this heavy trade and assess what it means for both the Maple Leafs and the Blue Jackets.

The Maple Leafs had a very busy offseason, but while new GM John Chayka did a lot of tinkering, it did not seem that he had yet quite changed the energy around the team.

Kirill Marchenko, 26, is a budding star who was held down by the talent around him in Columbus. His 27 goals and 40 assists in 76 games last season are impressive, given how little help he had; no other forward had more than 59 points, and only Adam Fantilli and Charlie Coyle broke the 40-point barrier.

It's not an ideal setup for any player, let alone one with Marchenko's toolbox. The Russian is 6'3" and is a convincing north-south skater. His puck skills are brilliant. Marchenko is also one of the league's best shooters from distance. His release is quick and effortless; he picks corners, and he disguises his intentions. Marchenko is a huge threat shooting from above the circles or in the high slot.

He is also a great driver of offense, creating many zone entries with his speed and skill. Aside from being flat-out better than Knies, he brings a skill set better suited to the Leafs' needs. He'll be able to run-and-gun with the likes of McKenna, Matthews, and Nylander, providing much more offensive upside. Nobody will replace Mitch Marner, but his presence has to be very reassuring to Auston Matthews as he figures out his future in Toronto.

The addition of winger Miles Wood also indicates a desire to address the Leafs' slow skating. He is in the top 10% of NHLers for 20+ MPH bursts. His $2.5 million contract through 2027 isn't ideal, but he's dealt with injuries in the past and could need a fresh start on a team where his role is clear.

It's familiar territory for Columbus. A top player wants out, and the team has to scramble to make lemonade out of lemons.

Considering they lacked much leverage — Marchenko is a restricted free agent next summer — and were looking to acquire players who could help now rather than future lottery tickets, the Blue Jackets come away from this at least having saved face.

Matthew Knies, 23, is a different type of player than Marchenko. He lacks the refined skills and speed that Marchenko has, but he drives play in his own right. Knies is very involved in touching pucks on the breakout. The left-winger is heavy, at 6'3" and 232 pounds, and he is aggressive on the forecheck. Knies is a pristine finisher around the net and has decent playmaking instincts. He'll fit well into a lot of different systems and with different linemates.

It's a major downgrade in talent. Marchenko is a bona fide first-line winger who could hit point-per-game numbers in Toronto; Knies, meanwhile, is better suited as a second-liner. Or, if he's on the top line, he needs to be the third-best player, tasked with more rustic duties. There's no Auston Matthews or William Nylander in Columbus. He is another player in a mold that Columbus had accumulated: strong middle-six play drivers who lack individual offensive upside.

Emil Andrae, not for nothing, is a good puck-moving defenseman who could fill in as a third-pairing defenseman. The 24-year-old is an analytical favorite, though he is just 5'9.

The Blue Jackets lose by virtue of trading Marchenko, but under the circumstances, GM Don Waddell did well enough. The biggest point of relief for the Blue Jackets will be that Knies is locked up at a reasonable $7.75 million cap hit through 2031. That's at least one young building block whom they won't have to worry about for the next few seasons. On top of that, they get some financial freedom by offloading Wood and part of Merzļikins' contract, as well as a second-round pick.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin is already somehow blaming the SEC's new conference schedule for LSU's injuries
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin is already blaming LSU's injuries on the SEC's new nine-game conference schedule, despite the Tigers having played just two league games.
articles.body: For years, the SEC has enjoyed a bit of an advantage over other conferences when it comes to record, rankings, and strength of schedule: they played fewer conference games. The Pac-12, when that conference existed in its previous form, for example, played nine games against other conference teams. So did the Big Ten. The SEC, however, had just eight. With four non-conference opponents, some schools could choose to schedule four likely wins, before entering SEC play. An ideal example is the 2025 Missouri Tigers. Missouri's non-conference slate was Central Arkansas, Kansas, Louisiana, and Massachusetts. Four games in which they'd be overwhelming favorites, four wins secured before conference play started. FLORIDA GATORS, MISSISSIPPI STATE SOAR, USC TUMBLES IN LATEST INEXPLICABLE AP TOP 25 POLL Missouri proceeded to win just four conference games, 29-20 over South Carolina, 23-17 over Auburn in double overtime, a 49-27 win over Mississippi State, and 31-17 over Arkansas. But, thanks in large part to their four scheduled wins, the Tigers remained in the AP Poll for most of the season, providing a "ranked" opponent for Texas A&M, Vanderbilt, Alabama, and Oklahoma. They did not beat a team that finished the season with a winning record on their way to finishing 8-4. Incredibly, with this resume, the Tigers were ranked in 12 of 16 polls during the regular season. And why not? 8-4 doesn't look bad, does it? That's a solid season in a tough conference, if you aren't paying close attention. Now remove one of those scheduled non-conference wins, and suddenly the road to 8-4 looks a lot harder. Which is the point other conferences made when arguing against the SEC's endless complaints about strength of schedule. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Well, for 2026, the SEC finally moved to nine conference games and eliminated the "extra" win many of the member programs used to their advantage. And even through just a few weeks of conference play, new LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin is already using it as an excuse. Ahead of last weekend's matchup against Texas A&M, Kiffin complained sarcastically, and inaccurately, about the perceived scheduling issues hurting the Tigers with Marcel "Obviously we just played the best one in the country last week thinking he can hurt you even when you have the right call on and everybody covered and a guy comes free," he said. "Obviously he (Chambliss) played great a year ago here in the stadium, so this is one of those scheduling quirks just like last week where never in that LSU-Ole Miss series had it ever been played two times in a row." That was, of course, incorrect, but Kiffin wasn't done there in going after the SEC for its scheduling practices. LSU is dealing with its fair share of injuries through the first few weeks of the season, including to star linebacker Whit Wheeks and tight end Trey'Dez Green. Per ESPN's Marty Smith, LSU's injuries are a direct result of the SEC's nine-game conference schedule. Which is odd because his team has played just two conference games so far. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. articles.title: Winners and Losers from the Kirill Marchenko-Matthew Knies Trade
articles.summary: Kirill Marchenko and Matthew Knies were the subject of trade rumors for most of the summer.
articles.body:
Kirill Marchenko and Matthew Knies were the subject of trade rumors for most of the summer.

On Monday, just one day before the start of the 2026-27 NHL season, they were both finally traded.

The Blue Jackets are sending Marchenko, Miles Wood, and goalie Elvis Merzlikins (with some retained salary) to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Knies, defenseman Emil Andrae, and Steven Lorentz.

The deal also comes with Marchenko signing a new long-term contract extension with Toronto.

Marchenko and Knies are obviously the focal points of the deal and the most consequential players involved, so let's take a look at some of the biggest winners and losers of the trade.

Marchenko is the biggest winner here simply because he managed to get everything he wanted.

It had become pretty clear over the past few weeks and months that he had no interest in signing a long-term deal with Columbus. Now he gets the fresh start and new team/city that he had been hoping for, while also cashing in on a six-year, $75 million contract that pays him $12.5 million per season.

Along with the change of scenery and new money, he also gets to play on a Toronto team loaded with high-level offensive talent, which could help him elevate his game and production to an even higher level.

He's always had great underlying numbers and strong production, and now he is joining a team that has Auston Matthews, William Nylander, John Tavares, and Gavin McKenna. They could work some offensive magic there. This will be by far some of the best offensive talent he has ever played with in his career.

This is not to say Columbus has lost this trade, or is a loser in the trade from a hockey perspective.

That is not the argument here. Not even close.

Matthew Knies is an outstanding player, and also a very different type of player from Marchenko. He's a big, strong power forward who has not only demonstrated the ability to be a top-line scorer but also to play a physical game and elevate his performance in big moments.

The latter part is something Columbus was badly lacking in 2025-26, down the stretch, when things got tough and adversity built. When head coach Rick Bowness went on his post-game rant after their Game 82 loss, he talked about needing to change the team's culture and mindset.

Maybe this is the type of move that does that.

But here's the problem from a perception standpoint: All anybody outside of Columbus is going to see here is a talented, in-their-prime player with star ability who did not want to re-sign there and ultimately wanted out.

That is a tough thing for your team and your city to have.

Against the backdrop of the uncertainty of Zach Werenski's future and the rumors that surrounded him this offseason, as well as the way Adam Fantilli's contract negotiations played out, it has not been a great offseason in Columbus. At least from a perception standpoint. And that does not even get into past situations involving star-level players like Artemi Panarin and Sergei Bobrovsky leaving in free agency, or a player like Jeff Carter making himself so miserable there that they had to quickly trade him shortly after acquiring him.

If you've ever been to a game in Columbus, you know it's a strong, very loyal fan base, given how little the organization has given them to get excited about over the years.

It's still a team that has not won a lot, and has not really had a ton of superstar players ... or been able to keep a lot of the superstar players that briefly came through the city.

The national and league-wide perception takes a hit from all of that.

The only way to change that perception is to win. Maybe Knies is the type of player who can help fix that.

Winner: Columbus' Long-Term Salary Cap Outlook

After finally signing Adam Fantilli to a long-term deal that pays him $13.5 million per season, Columbus found itself in a bit of a salary cap crunch going into the season that needed to be addressed.

While Marchenko was only set to earn $3.8 million this season, the $12.5 million contract extension represents a massive jump starting next season. He might be worth it. He's an excellent player. But that's still a big price tag for a first-line winger who might only top out as a second-tier star, and not quite a first-tier star. Even with the rising cap.

The Blue Jackets were also able to shed Miles Wood's $2.5 million per year over the next three years. It was by no means an albatross of a contract, but Wood wasn't really adding much either.

Columbus knows it is getting a really good winger back who will only take up $7.75 million against the cap through the 2031 season. Maybe you think Marchenko is a better player. He very well might be, and you certainly would not be wrong to hold that opinion. But do you like him for nearly $5 million extra dollars per year? Especially when Knies is a younger player and could, in theory, still improve from where he is now? Especially when you factor in the savings from dumping Wood's future contract?

1 Prospect Every Team Can Get Hyped About 🤩

Loser: David Pastrnak and the Boston Bruins

This is a weird little subplot you only catch if you pay attention to these things, but Boston could have really used a player like Marchenko, and there was plenty of smoke linking him to the Bruins.

Then this week, it was pointed out that Bruins players David Pastrnak and Nikita Zadorov started following Marchenko on social media , which is always the breeding ground for unfounded trade rumors.

And then Marchenko not only did not go to Boston, he went to a team in Boston's division.

Winner: Toronto's Offense and the Excitement Around It

Marchenko is going to be very expensive, and he has never quite played in the pressure cooker of a situation he will face with Toronto and the expectations that come with it. Especially as a $12.5 million-per-year player.

He is also older than Knies, and there is always some risk in trading a cheaper, younger player with comparable box score numbers for an older, more expensive player.

But objectively speaking, Marchenko is a better player in the short term (and perhaps the long term) and adds a lot to the Maple Leafs lineup that Knies does not, and might never, add.

Knies can play a physical, powerful game, but he is not the type of player who is going to really drive his own line or create a ton for himself. He will finish, score some tough goals, and aggressively forecheck. But he still needs some people around him to help drive the bus from a possession standpoint.

Marchenko can create more on his own. He is a better possession driver and is a more offensively skilled player and playmaker. There is a lot to be said for all of that.

Adding him to a lineup with Matthews, Nylander, Tavares, and McKenna could make this a potentially entertaining offense.

Whether or not that makes Toronto a better team remains to be seen. But it should certainly be a fun team, and that was another, lesser problem for the 2025-26 Maple Leafs. They were not only bad but also boring. Bad and boring is no way to go through a hockey season. The additions of McKenna, Marchenko, Darren Raddysh, and Sergei Bobrovsky at least add a little bit of juice to a team that was lacking it.

articles.title: Luke Littler: Defending champion stunned by Luke Woodhouse at World Grand Prix
articles.summary: World champion Luke Littler's hopes of defending his World Grand Prix title are dashed as he falls to a shock shock first-round defeat by Luke Woodhouse in Leicester.
articles.body:
World champion Luke Littler's hopes of defending his World Grand Prix title were dashed as he fell to a shock first-round defeat by Luke Woodhouse in Leicester.

Littler, 19, had been looking to bounce back from his quarter-final exit to Jonny Clayton at the World Series of Darts Finals just over a week ago.

But despite taking the first set, he was distinctly below par throughout the best-of-three encounter, averaging just 82.41.

That allowed Woodhouse to level the match and deliver a checkout of 75 to win the deciding set 3-1 in legs.

Woodhouse will face 2022 runner-up Nathan Aspinall in the last 16, who edged past Dutch debutant Kevin Doets 2-1.

Earlier on Monday, six-time winner Michael van Gerwen lost five legs out of the last six as 2024 semi-finalist Ryan Joyce fought back to win 2-1.

England's Joyce will play Dutchman Danny Noppert, who advanced past Germany's Niko Springer by the same scoreline.

Elsewhere, Wales' Gerwyn Price only lost a single leg as he comfortably beat Poland's Sebastian Bialecki 2-0 to set up a meeting with England's Ross Smith, who came from behind to triumph 2-1 against Scotland's Cameron Menzies.

Welshman Clayton edged past Krzysztof Ratajski 2-1, and he will take on the Netherlands' Wessel Nijman, who overcame 2018 world champion Rob Cross in straight sets.

articles.title: Arizona State hockey players ask school president to place coach on leave after workout left Matthew Mayich in a coma
articles.summary: Matthew Mayich collapsed during a workout last month and is now on live support and in a coma.
articles.body:
A group of Arizona State men's hockey players have written a letter asking the university to place head coach Greg Powers and his staff on administrative leave in the wake of a workout that left sophomore Matthew Mayich on life support and in a coma in August.

Seven Sun Devils players wrote a 26-page letter to Arizona State president Michael Crow on Monday, which was obtained by The Athletic . They wrote the letter anonymously through an attorney, as they said they fear retaliation from Powers.

The players disputed several findings from the university's initial review of the Aug. 20 workout that resulted in Mayich's collapse, including that he did not receive water and was provided inadequate medical care after collapsing.

"The head coach and his assistant coaches were all on the field on August 20, all remain in their positions, and together they decide our playing time, scholarship levels, and roster status," the players wrote. "No one has separated us from them since that morning. "We should not have to choose between telling the truth about August 20 and keeping what we have worked our whole lives for."

"The head coach and his assistant coaches were all on the field on August 20, all remain in their positions, and together they decide our playing time, scholarship levels, and roster status," the players wrote. "No one has separated us from them since that morning.

"We should not have to choose between telling the truth about August 20 and keeping what we have worked our whole lives for."

Mayich was participating in a workout with the team on Aug. 20 when he collapsed and later fell into a coma. The workout was described as "grueling" and run by an ex-U.S. Army Green Beret.

While an Arizona State report said players were given a water break around 20 minutes into the workout, the players who wrote the letter Monday said otherwise. A water break was given around 40 minutes into the 75-minute workout, but it lasted just seconds, according to the players. Only about eight players actually received water, they said, as they were the first who had just finished a bear crawl drill moments before.

"The first of us to finish had a few seconds at the bottles before being ordered back while others, including Matthew, were still crawling," players wrote. "This was the only water break."

At one point, they said, the Green Beret admitted to forgetting that players needed water and said that he didn't drink water during combat.

Mayich, they said, showed obvious signs of distress early in the workout. They said he became disoriented during the bear crawl, and could not carry a teammate during a buddy carry exercise. At one point, they said, he leaned on another teammate in order to stand up while a drill was being explained to them.

"No one at ASU properly monitored him during the workout and no one intervened," they wrote.

Once Mayich collapsed, they said, he remained in direct sunlight for several minutes. Unlike what Arizona State said in its report, which stated that Mayich remained on the ground, players said that he twice sat upright, once on the field and later when he was carried into the shade by teammates. The only cooling mechanisms there, they said, were small towels from a cooler, water from squirt bottles and water sprayed from a garden hose.

They also said the team did not properly acclimate players, including those from colder locations — Mayich is from Ontario — to the Arizona heat. The only outdoor workouts they did before Aug. 20, the players said, were roughly 15 minutes long.

"Matthew spent most of his 'off' time in his air-conditioned apartment because the heat was too oppressive for him," the players wrote.

Powers has led the Sun Devils for nearly two decades. He played goalie for them in the 1990s, and he led the team from the club level to an NCAA Division I program in 2015. He signed a five-year extension last November.

Powers was asked about the incident repeatedly last week, but refused to talk about it other than saying it's been "a difficult time" for the program. Powers, the players alleged, downplayed Mayich's condition initially and told them that he needed only an IV after suffering "just a little heat stroke." Powers also told them that they were "closer to making the Frozen Four because of the workout and Matthew having pushed himself to the maximum." The next day, they said, Powers told them that he had received "good news" and Mayich would be fine.

"From what we could tell, at no point did Coach Powers seem to appreciate the severity of the situation," the players wrote.

Mayich was selected by the St. Louis Blues in the sixth round of the 2023 NHL Draft. He transferred to Arizona State from Clarkson University (N.Y.) this past summer, and had previously played in the Ontario Hockey League. His l awyer said earlier this month that he has "zero chance of recovery."

Arizona State will open the season Friday at Lindenwood.

articles.title: Inspiring story on finding success together:“We both have dreams that we’re chasing, and we can relate around that"- How Lauren Kyle and Connor McDavid built careers beyond the rink
articles.summary: For Connor McDavid, success has always been measured in goals, assists, trophies and the pursuit of the Stanley Cup.
articles.body: For Connor McDavid, success has always been measured in goals, assists, trophies and the pursuit of the Stanley Cup. For Lauren Kyle McDavid, it has taken a different shape. Her world is built around interiors, fashion, hospitality and creating spaces people remember. Together, they have built something that reaches well beyond the Edmonton Oilers. Their story is not simply about a hockey superstar and his wife. It is about two ambitious people building separate careers while learning how to support each other through demanding goals, setbacks and new opportunities.Lauren Kyle McDavid built her own business identityLauren Kyle McDavid's career began long before she became known as Connor McDavid's wife. Her interest in design started early, and she studied interior design at Toronto Metropolitan University. After moving from Toronto to Edmonton in 2019, she launched Kyle & Co, an interior design studio that became the foundation for a much larger business portfolio.Her ambitions did not stop with residential design. Lauren later expanded into furniture, hospitality and fashion. Trove Living became a furniture showroom and a home for Kyle & Co, while Bar Trove added a hospitality arm to her growing business world. In 2026, the University of Alberta described her portfolio as including Kyle & Co, Trove Living, Bar Trove and Sports Club Atelier.That expansion says a lot about how Lauren approaches creativity. She has taken one interest and allowed it to lead naturally into another. Design influenced her furniture business. Her interest in sport helped shape her fashion brand. Hospitality gave her another way to turn design into an experience.Her philosophy is less about simply selling a product and more about creating an atmosphere.“It’s all about the feeling,” says Kyle McDavid, creating experiences that make people feel good and, ultimately, part of something bigger than themselves.That idea now runs through several parts of her professional life.Connor McDavid and Lauren Kyle share a drive to improveWhile Lauren has been building companies, Connor has continued to carry the enormous expectations that come with being the Edmonton Oilers captain and one of the NHL's biggest stars.Yet their careers are remarkably different. One revolves around competition on the ice. The other involves clients, employees, products, spaces and business decisions.Lauren has said that the difference does not make their ambitions harder to understand. Instead, it gives them common ground.“We both have dreams that we’re chasing, and we can relate around that,” she said. “We both know how we need to show up for each other in those moments and how we need to support each other in order to reach our goals. It’s really important to have a partner like that, who does understand and does provide support, because you need all the support you can get when he’s grinding through the playoffs and I’m grinding through opening businesses.”That perspective helps explain why their relationship works as more than a familiar sports celebrity story. Both understand what it means to have a demanding goal that requires consistency.Lauren has also described Connor as someone who has supported her entrepreneurial ambitions. Forbes reported that he gave her business-coaching sessions as a birthday gift, an early gesture that helped her develop the skills needed to manage a growing group of ventures.Lauren Kyle expanded from interiors into fashion and hospitalityOne of the most interesting parts of Lauren's career is how little she has treated her original field as a limit.Sports Club Atelier grew from her experience designing playoff jackets for the Oilers' wives and girlfriends. What began as a creative project developed into a sportswear business, with the brand moving beyond a single team and into broader sports partnerships. Forbes reported plans involving several NHL teams and Team Canada, while the University of Alberta later described the label as officially licensed with the NHL.Lauren's fashion work also reflects how she sees creativity. She does not treat interiors, clothing, art and sport as completely separate worlds.“I think, when you’re creative, you’re interested in everything that that inspires you creatively,” she said. “For me, I look at fashion to inspire my interiors, everything overlaps each other. So it’s natural that I would be interested in art, fashion. Anything that gets my creative mind going.”Bar Trove added another dimension. Located in downtown Edmonton, the space combines hospitality with Lauren's design sensibility. When the project was announced, CityNews reported that the venture was entering an area where downtown businesses were facing an evolving commercial environment.For Lauren, the challenge was not simply opening another venue. It was creating somewhere people would deliberately choose to visit.That philosophy remains central to her approach. In 2026, she told Alberta School of Business students that a physical business cannot rely only on foot traffic. Instead, she said, it needs to become a destination through careful attention to details such as lighting, music, food and service.Connor McDavid and Lauren Kyle built a partnership around ambitionAway from the businesses and hockey games, their relationship has developed alongside their professional lives. The pair met through a family connection when McDavid was a teenager, and their relationship grew while both were beginning important chapters in their lives. Lauren eventually moved to Edmonton and built her career there, while Connor became the face of the Oilers franchise.Lauren has also spoken about the pressure that comes with being connected to professional hockey. She pushed back against the assumption that being an NHL player's wife is simple, pointing to the demands and strain that can exist away from the public view.The couple's approach to mistakes offers another window into their shared mindset.“We both are leaders in a sense. He’s a captain on his team. I manage different employees. And although our careers are so different, the principles are the same … Mistakes are great. They expose gaps. And then you work on constantly improving and finding gaps.”That may be the clearest thread connecting their careers. Connor's world demands constant improvement on the ice. Lauren's businesses demand the same discipline away from it.Lauren's own approach has evolved as her companies have grown. In 2026, she told Alberta School of Business students that she has learned to remain closely involved in vision and creative direction while giving her team more ownership over execution.That shift is significant. Building a business is not just about having good ideas. It is about turning those ideas into something that can function without the founder controlling every detail.For Connor and Lauren, success therefore looks different but follows a similar rhythm. One prepares for another NHL season. The other develops new brands and businesses. One faces the pressure of a packed arena. The other faces the pressure of building something from the ground up.Their story is ultimately about partnership without losing individuality. Connor McDavid continues to pursue his ambitions in hockey, while Lauren Kyle McDavid has created a growing business identity of her own. articles.title: Arizona State Hockey Players Send Letter to School President About Teammate's Collapse
articles.summary: TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — Seven members of Arizona State's hockey team have sent a letter to the school president calling for the coaching staff to be placed on administrative leave until an independent investigation into the collapse of a teammate is completed.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — Seven members of Arizona State's hockey team have sent a letter to the school president calling for the coaching staff to be placed on administrative leave until an independent investigation into the collapse of a teammate is completed.

The letter sent to President Michael Crow through an attorney on Monday also contradicted some of the facts stated in Arizona State's initial probe into the collapse of Matthew Mayich during an outdoor workout on Aug. 20.

The players sent the letter anonymously through attorney Timothy J. Casey out of fear of retaliation. The letter said several other members of the team share their concerns and questions, but opted to not join the letter for fear of retaliation for speaking the truth.

"We are submitting this report anonymously because we fear retaliation from the coaching staff," the letter said. "That fear is not directed at one person. The head coach and his assistant coaches were all on the field on August 20, all remain in their positions, and together they decide our playing time, scholarship levels, and roster status. No one has separated us from them since that morning."

Mayich, a defenseman who was drafted by the St. Louis Blues, collapsed during an outdoor workout on the first day the NCAA allows teams to hold formal activities. He remains hospitalized and his family's attorney has said the 21-year-old is unlikely to recover after suffering exertional heat stroke that reduced flow of oxygen to his brain.

The Arizona State police department is investigating the incident and a report will be sent to the Maricopa County Attorney's Office for independent review when completed.

Arizona's House and Senate education committee chairs called for an independent investigation of Arizona State's hockey workout after reading the letter from the players.

"Seven players who were on that field have raised serious questions that ASU's own review does not answer," House education committee chairman Matt Gress said. "We need an independent investigation to determine whether ASU followed its own rules, who was responsible for protecting these athletes, and what happened when Matthew Mayich showed signs of distress. ASU should not be left to investigate its own conduct and decide whether anyone should be held accountable."

Arizona State's initial report showed ASU hockey coaches were present during the workout, but plans for the training session were not submitted to the school.

The players' letter claims multiple parts of ASU exertional heat policy were not followed before and after Mayich collapsed, including progressive acclimatization to Arizona's heat, frequent rest periods and access to fluids whenever needed.

The letter said the workout was 75 minutes of constant exertion and only the players who did well at the task were allowed a break for liquids. Mayich was not among the players who were allowed to hydrate, it said.

The letter said Mayich appeared to be disoriented much earlier than the ASU report said and was not properly cooled before paramedics arrived. It also said coach Greg Powers downplayed the severity of Mayich's condition, telling players he had "just a little heat stroke" and told the players he would be fine before practice the next day.

The players called for the staff responsible for approving, conducting and supervising the session be placed on administrative leave and name an interim coaching staff. It also called for the investigation to be referred to an agency outside of the university.

"An interim staff would allow the investigation to be completed and the players to be heard, without asking players to put their scholarships, roster positions, and playing time at risk in order to be heard," the letter said. "It is not fair to require that."

The Blues drafted Mayich in the sixth round of the 2023 NHL draft, but he never signed an entry-level contract. The Stoney Creek, Ontario, native played four seasons with the Ottawa 67's of the Ontario Hockey League before playing at Clarkson University last season.

Mayich transferred to Arizona State for the upcoming season.

articles.summary: On the heels of AAA Worlds Collide, WWE Raw hit the Netflix airwaves, live from the Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee with a jam-packed broadcast.
articles.body:
On the heels of AAA Worlds Collide, WWE Raw hit the Netflix airwaves, live from the Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee with a jam-packed broadcast.

What went down when LA Knight, Oba Femi, Women's World Champion Stephanie Vaquer, and other to red brand Superstars were in the building?

Find out with this recap of the September 28 show, including grades, reaction, and highlights from each match.

Announced in advance of the night's show were:

Appearances from Knight, Femi, and Vaquer

Last Time in Action: The Usos fought LA Knight and Solo Sikoa to a no contest (Raw, August 24); Jacob Fatu defeated Royce Keys in a Street Fight (Raw, August 3)

A fired-up Bloodline kicked off the show, with Jacob Fatu and The Usos addressing 946's kidnapping of Solo Sikoa on last week's show.

Jimmy said they may have their differences, but Sikoa is still his brother. Fatu said he was wrong to hold back the twins in recent weeks, and now their issues with 946 are on-sight.

Jey issued their warning shot before all three took off backstage to the parking garage, ready to confront Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, and Lucian Price. Instead, they were met by NXT's Jaida Parker, who said she was there to meet with Adam Pearce.

The fire shown across the board here was excellent. Jimmy told the story expertly, reminding the audience that blood trumps all, despite the intense rivalry they have had with Sikoa over the years.

Parker showing up, and the awkward exchange with Jey, was a nice touch and plays on rumors and innuendo that everyone is already aware of.

Last Time in Action: Lola Vice defeated Kelani Jordan and Raquel Rodriguez (Raw, September 14); Roxanne Perez defeated La Catalina and Iyo Sky (Raw, September 21)

Vice and Perez will battle in the Money in the Bank Ladder Match. Before they do, they squared off in a one-on-one bout Monday night.

Late in the match, Perez cut off Vice's comeback attempt, delivering a lionsault for two and immediately segueing into the crossface. The babyface fought out and transitioned into an armbar.

Perez fought free but ultimately walked into the MIA spinning backfist as Vice scored the win.

After the match, Raquel Rodriguez attacked until Sol Ruca made the save. Perez halted her momentum, though, and the Judgment Day left the babyfaces lying to close out the segment.

The match itself was good and highlighted the chemistry between Perez and Vice that was forged in the rings of NXT.

The post-match beatdown was the right call and helped re-establish Perez's momentum, which was unnecessarily damaged by the loss. Could Rodriguez not get there in advance to cause a disqualification and spare The Prodigy the loss?

Ruca desperately needs new theme music. Like, yesterday.

Last Time in Action: Oba Femi defeated Bron Breakker via DQ (Sunday Night's Main Event, September 6)

The Ruler hit the ring, dressed in casual wear and carrying a contract.

He said there was business to attend to and called out Bronson Reed.

The Auszilla answered the challenge, coming to the ring sans The Vision. Unintimidated by the big man, Reed said that each time they have shared the ring, he has left Femi lying.

He signed the contract for a match at Money in the Bank in New Orleans.

"I know, I know...he sucks," was a great bit from Femi and hinted that the big man has charisma and natural mic abilities that will get him over far more organically, not to mention quicker, than sticking to a script.

Reed was great on the mic. He wasted no words, got his point across, and sold the match.

Last Time in Action: Dragon Lee lost to Penta (Raw, September 21); Big Cass defeated Josh Briggs (Raw, September 24)

Seeking revenge after finding himself on the receiving end of a Big Cass beatdown, Lee took the fight to the giant right from the opening bell.

Big Cass dominated the action through the commercial break, however, and was in a good position to earn a win late. Lee showed tremendous resiliency, though, and fought his way back into the match.

He launched himself through the ropes, wiped him out at ringside, and countered a fireman's carry into a modified octopus. From there, he set up for Enter the Dragon, but Cass countered and tried for a chokeslam. Lee countered it, stacked his larger opponent up, and scored the win.

This was the best Cass has looked yet since returning to WWE. He has repeatedly been tested against smaller, quicker opponents and here, against Lee, he was right there with the luchador at every spot and never looked out of place.

Lee is one of the most dynamic, exciting young stars on the roster, he is finally getting the spotlight and is making the most of it.

Backstage, Stephanie Vaquer announced a No. 1 Contender's Match next week between Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan for a shot at her Women's World Championship.

Last Time in Action: Iyo Sky lost to Roxanne Perez (Raw, September 21); Lyra Valkyria defeated Bayley (Raw, September 21)

Born of a backstage confrontation, two of the best wrestlers in WWE squared off as Valkyria clashed with Sky.

After the commercial, Sky looked to turn the tide in her favor with a Bullet Train atack, only for Valkyria to rock her with an enzuigiri, followed by a gut-wrench suplex, and cover for two.

Sky countered the Nightwing and delivered a delayed underhook backbreaker for another new-fall.

Valkyria recovered and threatened to win the match, but Sky weathered the storm and set her up for the Over the Moonsault. Valkyria met her up top and brought her down for another near-fall.

articles.title: “Greatest gift”: Ashlyn Harris reveals why Sophia Bush and their children have become her greatest source of happiness
articles.summary: For Ashlyn Harris, the most meaningful part of her relationship with Sophia Bush is not something that can be bought or planned. It is time.
articles.body: For Ashlyn Harris, the most meaningful part of her relationship with Sophia Bush is not something that can be bought or planned. It is time. The former USWNT goalkeeper opened up about what she values most in her relationship with the One Tree Hill actress while attending the inaugural A Sense of Home Gala in New York City on Sept. 23. Harris and Bush, who began dating in 2023, also brought Harris’ two children to the event. The evening gave Harris a chance to reflect on family, giving back and the simple moments that have helped shape their life together.Ashlyn Harris calls time the greatest gift in her relationship with Sophia BushHarris, 40, said time is the “greatest gift” she has found in her relationship with Bush, 44. She pointed out that it comes without a financial cost, making it even more meaningful as their busy lives continue to involve work, travel and family commitments.“And it comes at zero cost,” she told PEOPLE while stepping out with Bush, 44, at the inaugural A Sense of Home Gala in New York City on Wednesday, Sept. 23.The couple also used the event as an opportunity to teach Harris’ children about helping others. Harris shares daughter Sloane, 5, and son Ocean, 4, with her ex-wife, former soccer star Ali Krieger.Rather than simply bringing the children along, Harris sees these public appearances as chances to help them understand the value of community service.“We try to teach them, more importantly than anything, that acts of service and acts of kindness go a really long way,” she explained. “And they’re lucky enough to be born into a bit of privilege, so it’s important for us to show them at a very early age that it’s our job to give back and to serve other families and other communities, ones that look like us, ones that don’t look like us.”She continued, “So for us, it’s important to bring them to places like this for them to understand the importance of showing up for other people and making sure they serve their community.”Sophia Bush and Ashlyn Harris build a blended family around togethernessHarris also offered a glimpse into how she and Bush define home. With demanding schedules and frequent travel, she said their idea of home is less about a physical location and more about being together.“We’re two moms who work incredibly hard to give our children a better life than we had. What I’m learning with our hectic travel schedule is home is where we all are when we’re all together. That’s all that matters to us.”She explained, “It’s definitely not a place — it’s the feeling we get when we’re a collective. And that’s what matters the most to Sophia and me.”Their relationship began after both women had gone through major changes in their personal lives. Bush later revealed that the pair first connected through a group chat with friends navigating breakups. What started as friendship eventually became something more.In an earlier interview with PEOPLE, Harris described Bush as “the best thing that ever happened” to her, adding, “She’s an absolute delight, and my kids love her. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian chess grandmaster Divya Deshmukh was named Best Chess Player (Female) at the inaugural FIDE Excellence Awards in recognition of her
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian chess grandmaster Divya Deshmukh was named Best Chess Player (Female) at the inaugural FIDE Excellence Awards in recognition of her outstanding performances over the past year, headlined by her spectacular victory at the Women’s World Cup, with India also completing a hat-trick of Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy triumphs. Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov was named Best Chess Player (Male).The award added to a strong showing by the Indian contingent, with the country’s Open and Women’s National Teams also recognised as Best Team for having the most combined points out of all natons in this 46th edition of Olympiad. The All India Chess Federation (AICF) finished third in the Best Federation category.India retained the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy for the third consecutive Olympiad, following its victories at Chennai in 2022 and Budapest in 2024.The Open team won silver, while the Women’s team secured bronze, alongside six individual medals for Indian players.Reflecting on the achievements, AICF President Nitin Narang said, “This is an immensely proud moment for Bharat and for Indian chess. To bring home the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy for the third consecutive Olympiad, along with silver in the Open section, bronze in the Women’s section and six individual medals, is a remarkable achievement. From Chennai to Budapest and now Samarkand, our players have consistently made the Tricolour fly high on the global stage. My heartiest congratulations to every member of Team India for once again making the entire nation proud.”Narang also pointed to the wider recognition earned by Indian chess, including Divya’s individual honour and the awards for the national teams, federation and chess content.“What makes Samarkand even more special is the recognition India has received across the wider chess ecosystem. From our players and national teams to the federation and chess content, Indian chess is making its presence felt across every dimension of the sport," he added."This is a celebration of the collective effort of our players, coaches, families, administrators, organisers, creators and the entire chess community. India is not only producing champions; we are building a chess ecosystem that is earning recognition across the world.”He also acknowledged the wider team behind India’s success.“Achievements of this magnitude are never individual efforts. Our captains, coaches, seconds and support staff have worked tirelessly behind the scenes, while the families and parents of our players have been an integral part of their journeys. Every member of this contingent has contributed to what India has achieved in Samarkand, and I congratulate and thank them all.”The Samarkand campaign also leaves Indian chess with two major World Championship contests to look forward to, with D Gukesh set to defend his crown and R Vaishali preparing to challenge for the Women’s World Championship.“Indian chess is going through an extraordinary phase, and there is much more to look forward to. articles.title: From Jamshedpur slum to Asian Games: Joga Purty’s unlikely climb to India’s speed climbing record
articles.summary: Kolkata: When Joga Purty first walked into the climbing wall at JRD Tata Sports Complex in Jamshedpur, she had no idea what sport climbing was.
articles.body: Kolkata: When Joga Purty first walked into the climbing wall at JRD Tata Sports Complex in Jamshedpur, she had no idea what sport climbing was.A friend had suggested she tag along, and curiosity brought her there. Nearly seven years later, the 19-year-old from a modest family in Jamshedpur is India’s national record holder in speed climbing and on her way to the Asian Games.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal Tally“I never thought I would get an opportunity to compete at the Asian Games,” said Purty, who will make her debut in women’s speed climbing at the continental showpiece in Japan on Tuesday.“To be honest, my reaction was quite normal. I didn’t know much about the Games then, and I had already travelled for international competitions, so I didn’t think of it as something very different.”The Asiad may be her biggest stage yet, but the teenager’s journey has been anything but straightforward.Her father, Nandu, runs a small shop while her mother, Jhana, works as a domestic help. The youngest among three siblings, it was initially difficult for Purty to convince her family and neighbours that climbing was worth pursuing.“Joga comes from a humble background and grew up in the slum area. In the early days, she would often miss training sessions. I used to visit her home and speak to her parents to convince them to let her come for practice,” said Bibhas Roy, who trained her at Tata Steel Adventure Foundation (TSAF) Climbing Academy before moving to Bengaluru as India’s national coach in 2024.But the turning point came when she won medals in all three climbing disciplines at a national championship before the Covid-19 pandemic. “When my photo appeared in the newspapers, my mother became very proud. After that, nobody questioned my participation anymore,” she recalled.Although Purty initially competed in all three disciplines of sport climbing — boulder, lead and speed — her coaches soon recognised where her true potential lay. “Once we realised she was excelling in speed climbing, we decided to focus entirely on that discipline,” Roy said.The move quickly brought results. Purty announced herself on the international stage by winning a silver medal at 2024 IFSC Asian Youth Climbing Championships.Since then, she has represented India at World Championships and 2026 Asian Climbing Championships, while repeatedly lowering her own national record. Her current national mark of 7.37 seconds sealed her place in India’s Asian Games squad.Ahead of the Asian Games, Purty spent two months training in Indonesia before attending a camp in Thailand. While Roy admits Purty’s timings did not improve as much as expected during the latest overseas stint, he remains convinced that her best days lie ahead.“Her biggest strengths are her natural power and explosive speed. If she continues training properly and remains disciplined, I believe she can break into the six-second range within the next year,” he said.Climbing is also an expensive sport and for Purty, support from the Tata Steel Adventure Foundation has played a key role in keeping her climbing dream alive. A good pair of climbing shoes costs around Rs 10,000 and typically lasts only three to six months depending on usage. A harness can cost upwards of Rs 11,000, while chalk bags and chalk powder add significantly to the expenses.Competition at the Asian Games, however, will be fierce, with climbers from Kazakhstan, Indonesia, China and hosts Japan among the favourites. Yet Roy believes his protégé has the qualities required to compete with the continent’s best.“She has a very bright future and the potential to qualify for the Olympics one day,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
SAN ANGELO, Texas ( Concho Valley Homepage ) — The Angelo State University football team was hungry for the first win of the 2026 season this past Saturday, and the Rams were able to pull it off.

ASU outlasted No. 17 Western Oregon 29-28 in overtime in Eugene, Oregon. It was the longest road trip of the season, and it was well worth it for the Rams.

The Rams improved to 1-3 overall and 1-1 in the Lone Star Conference, while dropping the Wolves to 2-2 and 0-2.

ASU quarterback Ayden Arp had a great performance, completing 28 of 44 passes for 280 yards and four touchdowns.

The Wolves got the ball first in overtime and scored a touchdown, and then it was the Rams' turn.

Arp threw a 12-yard TD strike to Alan Dobbins in the overtime period, getting the Rams within 28-27. And instead of kicking the PAT to force a second overtime session, ASU opted to roll the dice and go for a two-point try and end the game right there.

And that's exactly what the Rams did, as Arp found Trevor Winn in the end zone for the game-winning PAT reception.

And now the Rams will try to treat their fans to the first home win of the season when they face defending LSC champion No. 14 Central Washington at 6 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 3 at LeGrand Stadium.

articles.title: Ryen Russillo praises Tom Brady for ‘being critical in a way where it’s not nasty’ in Fox booth
articles.summary: Tom Brady has considerably improved each season as an analyst for Fox Sports, and this year appears to be no different. During the Chargers-Bills broadcast o...
articles.body:
Tom Brady has considerably improved each season as an analyst for Fox Sports, and this year appears to be no different.

During the Chargers-Bills broadcast on Sunday, Brady became the most high-profile commentator to highlight Los Angeles's offensive shortcomings. As the Chargers puked up a 16-point performance to move to 0-3, Brady hammered the team repeatedly from the booth.

The criticism showed just how broken the team's offense may, but also showcased Brady's improvements as a game analyst, as noted by Ryen Russillo on a Monday episode of his podcast .

"That's what I thought was just brilliant about Brady on that broadcast," Russillo said. "He let every one of us know he was just disgusted with what they were doing on offense, but it never felt nasty. But it still felt like a more critical way that was entertaining, which I think some guys never get to in that spot."

The Chargers were supposed to take a step forward under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, but instead have regressed. The heralded 28-year-old quarterback Justin Herbert has more interceptions than touchdowns and is tipping from polarizing toward unpopular among analysts.

Rather than going on a rant intended to go viral or prove his superiority, Brady relentlessly pointed out poor play-calling and decision-making from McDaniel and Herbert, respectively. Along the way, Russillo noted, Brady also didn't hesitate to praise Herbert's physical ability. The fair, nuanced critique helped viewers understand the Chargers' struggles and why it is so disappointing.

"He is already the best at being critical in a way where it's not nasty," Russillo said. "Now, some guys will just not be critical. Or they give you the cliche, and you're like OK that's not going to happen. I actually would prefer somebody to be like, 'That's not going to work, what the f*ck are you doing?' I don't know if we'll ever get there in broadcasting. Certainly not on a network. But Brady's disdain for what the Chargers are on offense was so entertaining."

In recent seasons, ESPN's Troy Aikman has become known for letting the negativity fly . Audiences tend to appreciate this mentality because it shows commentators aren't worried about their relationships in the league or how colleagues view them. It is easy to see when analysts don't trust their judgment or know they may work in the league again. Brady is as respected and knowledgeable as anyone, which may make it easier for him to relax , trust his instincts, and be critical when it is called for.

Many assumed that once Brady learned the pacing of broadcasting, he would improve. That happened very quickly . Now, Brady is in the conversation for the best working game analyst. As Russillo notes, his ability to fairly dress down teams when they play poorly shows he is still getting better.

articles.body:
Former Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Andy Dalton entered the Eagles - Bears Monday Night Football game in relief of Eagles QB Jalen Hurts , and threw an interception in the end zone in the second quarter.

Dalton's first pass attempt of the 2026 season was picked by the Bears ' Dillon Thieneman.

With the Eagles trailing 7-0, Hurts had to leave the game for evaluation after he was hit out of bounds by the Bears' D'Marco Jackson.

Hurts screamed on the sideline, apparently over the amount of time it took to clear him to re-enter the game.

Earlier in the month, Dalton, who was vying to back up Hurts, earned the No. 2 job over third-stringer Tanner McKee when McKee was among the team's inactives for their season opener.

Dalton was 12-of-19 for 104 passing yards with a touchdown during the team's third and final preseason game against his former team, the Cincinnati Bengals , at Lincoln Financial Field.

Dalton, Cincinnati's starting QB from 2011 to 2019, ranks second behind Ken Anderson among Cincinnati's all-time leaders in passing yardage.

In March, Dalton was traded by the Carolina Panthers to Philly for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick.

Dalton, 38, played in 13 games over the past three seasons for the Panthers.

Dalton started against the Bengals during the 2024 season for the fourth time since Cincinnati released him in 2020.
