articles.title: A's season derailed by injuries and Kotsay calls it unlike anything he's seen
articles.summary: The Athletics entered the season with high hopes, and for good reason.  Mark Kotsay said Monday it was unlike anything he has seen in his five seasons as man...
articles.body:
The Athletics entered the season with high hopes, and for good reason.

They had a young core of talented players and came off a season in which they put together a 35-29 record after the All-Star break. The A's also played in baseball's worst division, the AL West, which Houston ultimately won with a .500 mark .

But then the injuries happened. Mark Kotsay said Monday it was unlike anything he has seen in his five seasons as manager.

"Even as a player, I can't recall a roster of your top five opening day players in the lineup going down and not having them for 60-plus games," said Kotsay, who played 17 big league seasons.

The injuries — as well as a pitching staff that struggled to keep balls inside the Athletics' temporary, hitter-friendly Triple-A stadium in West Sacramento, California — took a toll. Instead of making a playoff run, the A's went 64-98. Only Colorado and the Los Angeles Angels posted worse records.

"We didn't win enough games and we're not satisfied with the overall results," interim general manager Dan Feinstein said. "We came into the year expecting to contend, and obviously that didn't happen. At the same time, we made real progress in some important areas, and we saw continued growth from a number of our young players who were frankly thrust into some unexpected roles."

Feinstein pointed specifically to infielders Zack Gelof and Joshua Kuroda-Grauer and outfielder Henry Bolte making the most of their chances, which could benefit the A's when they play their scheduled third and final season in Sacramento before the club's planned move to Las Vegas in 2028 .

A potential lockout hangs over the start of next season, but Feinstein said the A's are proceeding as if everything is on schedule.

This season showed the unexpected could certainly create negative consequences.

Nick Kurtz , Brent Rooker , Jacob Wilson , Shea Langeliers and Tyler Soderstrom were on the injured list for a combined 340 games. Only Langeliers among that group finished the season, and the catcher did it as a designated hitter.

The A's also placed infielder Max Muncy on the IL with a knee injury last week.

Starting pitcher Luis Severino was placed on the IL on May 30 because of strained right shoulder and never took the mound again. Severino signed a $67 million, three-year contract in December 2024, but can opt out after this season. The right-hander is 10-17 with a 4.43 ERA in his short time with the A's.

"It's ultimately his decision," Feinstein said. "I don't want to get ahead of it. We've enjoyed having him here and once he makes his decision, we'll have a better sense of what the next steps are."

As far as next steps with other players, Kurtz and Rooker took batting practice late in the season and Kotsay said he expected a "normal" offseason for them. Wilson and Soderstrom are going through the rehabilitation process through winter, and Muncy's knee needs to be "further evaluated," the manager said.

Feinstein said the A's, as they routinely do, will evaluate every aspect of their organization now that the season is over, including the training and medical staffs.

But Kotsay said there wasn't a unifying reason why the A's had some many players get hurt.

"For Luis Severino going out and playing the WBC, you always question the intensity that he threw at so early in the year as to possibly leading to his injury," Kotsay said. "Shea Langeliers was a specific play. Tyler Soderstrom was a specific play.

"So if we're looking at strength and conditioning, training staff, medical as a cause, I think you have to look at the injury specific as opposed to the training methods. Generally, the training methods lead to muscle strains, in particular lower-half hamstrings, things of that nature. Correct me if I'm wrong, but elbow, things like of that nature in our arm care programs have held up really well in this organization."

articles.title: 3 bold predictions for White Sox-Astros AL Wild Card Series
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox and Houston Astros reached the postseason through different routes. The White Sox went 84-78, two years after losing 121 games. The Ast...
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox and Houston Astros reached the postseason through different routes. The White Sox went 84-78, two years after losing 121 games. The Astros won the American League West crown at 81-81, becoming the first division champion without a winning record. Yet the Astros won five of seven meetings between the clubs this season.

Their best-of-three AL Wild Card Series begins Tuesday at 5 p.m. ET at Daikin Park. The winner faces the Cleveland Guardians . Here are three predictions for a matchup in which Game 1 and the final result could tell different stories.

White Sox take Game 1 in a battle of bullpens

Astros manager Joe Espada will use a bullpen game, with AJ Blubaugh opening for Houston . Blubaugh led major league relievers with 96 innings this season and posted a 3.66 ERA. Chicago will counter with rookie left-hander Hagen Smith after using its leading starters over the weekend.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Neither club has a conventional Game 1 starter. The Astros want Blubaugh and their other arms to bridge the gap to Bryan Abreu and Josh Hader . The White Sox want their lineup to capitalize before those late-inning specialists take over.

Miguel Vargas hit 33 homers and drew 101 walks. Munetaka Murakami added 35 homers as a rookie. Blubaugh held the White Sox scoreless over four regular-season innings, but opening a playoff game presents a different challenge. One mistake with a runner aboard could decide it. Chicago strikes first and puts Houston one loss from elimination.

Murakami hits the series' defining home run

Murakami's swing-and-miss risk makes him an uneasy postseason centerpiece. He also has the power to turn one swing into the image everyone remembers. After a second-half slump, he hit four homers over his final 10 regular-season games and posted a 1.062 OPS in that span.

His surge included a two-homer game against Colorado on Friday. That finish makes a breakthrough plausible despite the pressure of his first MLB playoff appearance. Houston's shifting Game 1 pitching assignments could offer Murakami one pitch he can drive before the Astros reach their best relievers.

Murakami homers in his postseason debut , delivering a go-ahead shot in a White Sox Game 1 victory. It becomes the series' signature swing, even if it does not send the White Sox on to the ALDS to face the Guardians.

The opener represents Chicago's clearest chance to seize control. Wednesday brings Hunter Brown . Houston's ace posted a 1.38 ERA across two starts against the White Sox this season and is lined up for Game 2 on four days' rest. He finished the year with a 3.19 ERA and gives Espada the strongest starting-pitching advantage in this series.

Brown keeps the White Sox power bats quiet and forces a deciding game. Hayden Wesneski would be on schedule to start Thursday, while the Astros can turn to their veteran lineup at home. Yordan Alvarez led the majors with a 1.033 OPS and hit 42 homers. Hader converted all 26 save chances.

Chicago lands the first punch, but Brown restores Houston's footing. The Astros take Game 3 at Daikin Park and advance, 2-1.

articles.summary: Damian Lillard has no worries about his physical condition upon finishing his Achilles rehab ahead of the Portland Trail Blazers’ 2026-27 campaign. Lillard...
articles.body:
Damian Lillard has no worries about his physical condition upon finishing his Achilles rehab ahead of the Portland Trail Blazers ' 2026-27 campaign.

Lillard has been playing in the NBA since 2012, going through his 12th season with the Blazers. After two seasons with the Milwaukee Bucks, the team chose to waive and stretch the remainder of his contract as he ended up reuniting with Portland.

Lillard used the entire 2025-26 season to rehab his Achilles. While he took part in the 3-point shooting contest in All-Star Weekend, he spent all of the campaign to get his physical ability back up to speed.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Lillard took part in the team's Media Day on Monday, conversing with media throughout the afternoon. When reporters asked about his health, the veteran star guard expressed confidence about his athleticism and ability to produce on the court.

"I don't have any restrictions," Lillard said, via ESPN. "I talk about the injury when I'm asked about it, but when I'm playing, it's not a thought anymore. I'm at that stage. I'm able to play free."

"I'm capable of doing whatever I need to do, but at this stage, I don't think I need to kill myself in a regular season trying to play 37, 36, 35 minutes if it's unnecessary. We got a lot of guards, we got a lot of ability at the guard position, and I don't think it should be necessary for me to have to play 35 minutes."

What lies ahead for Damian Lillard, Blazers this season

Damian Lillard is on a mission to show he can ball out despite coming off injury rehab. And even though the Blazers have a logjam in the backcourt, he remains optimistic about the squad's chances of success this season.

"If we are just doing the right thing, playing the right way … I think the balance will work itself out," Lillard said, when asked how the team will deploy newly-acquired, former All-Star guard Ja Morant , former lottery pick Scoot Henderson and two-time NBA champion Jrue Holiday.

"If our mentality is right and we handle it right, I think we could be a tough time for everybody. If I get the ball and I'm advancing the ball ahead to Ja Morant, I feel pretty good about it. If I'm advancing the ball to [All-Star forward] Deni [Avdija] out there, I feel good about it. And for both of those guys, if they are attacking the rim, attacking the paint and they're kicking the ball out to me for a 3-pointer, I think they should feel great about that."

Portland will get its campaign underway with four preseason contests, starting and ending with the Golden State Warriors on Oct. 7 and Oct. 16. Their regular season will begin at home when they host the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 21 at 10 p.m. ET.

articles.title: David Stearns takes responsibility for disastrous Mets season
articles.summary: NEW YORK — At the conclusion of a disastrous season, David Stearns was faced with two options: Move forward without acknowledging the mess of 2026, or take r...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — At the conclusion of a disastrous season, David Stearns was faced with two options: Move forward without acknowledging the mess of 2026, or take responsibility for it.

The Mets president of baseball operations chose the latter option, showing a more human side Monday at Citi Field.

Admitting failure isn't easy, especially when you preside over a baseball team with an annual payroll north of $350 million. In doing so, it showed fans what he learned from the mistakes of 2026, and how the club plans to address them this winter.

"I think as we reflected on how the start of the season went the way it did, we and I made a number of decisions that created the potential for almost like an uncapped downside scenario," Stearns said. "We had a lot of change. We've talked about that. I think change in New York is probably different than change in other markets."

The Mets finished 74-88, last place in the NL East. Their -32 run differential was the fourth-worst in the National League. A perfect storm of forces brought the Mets down, but these weren't exactly outside elements. The Mets weren't prepared for injuries and underperformance.

There was a sweeping overhaul of the coaching staff and the roster. The Mets let key clubhouse leaders go and replaced them with players who were unproven in the game's toughest market. His free agent signings didn't work out the way he thought they would.

"I think we've had some that have worked out well, and clearly we've missed, and I've missed," he said. "If we look at last offseason, we missed too much. I certainly understand that."

It took longer than expected for the team to find any sort of spark, and the roster wasn't flexible enough to withstand injuries to stars like Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor , and the team crumbled under the weight of expectations.

"We weren't able to get ourselves out of it the way we should have or could have," Stearns said, "[Or] in a way that would have allowed us to, frankly, have a more productive entirety of the season."

The team played at a mostly .500 pace after firing manager Carlos Mendoza and replacing him with farm director Andy Green. The Mets showed real progress in the second half of the season, capitalizing on the parts of their game where they were already strong. They got great production out of key rookies, and the production of several veterans increased as well. Finally, the team came together.

Everyone got better and played better in the second half with the goal of laying the foundation for a more successful 2027 campaign.

The question now becomes: how can Stearns be sure that second-half surge wasn't just an aberration?

"One, you have the prospect pedigree that backs it up. Two, a lot of them, in my opinion, were doing it, frankly, under sort of extreme pressurized situation in the first half of the year when things were spinning sideways on us a little bit, and they were still showing up to the park every single day and performing," Stearns said. "So I do think it's real."

Stearns admitted he missed on too many free agents last winter, including at first base, where the Mets had steady production for years with Pete Alonso , and got almost none from Jorge Polanco . Alonso, the most beloved player to wear a Mets jersey since David Wright , hit his 300th home run at Citi Field against the Mets earlier in the month.

In a scene that was equal parts stunning and embarrassing for the Mets, fans were cheering for an opposing player, following them up with chants of "Fire Stearns."

"The truth is, in this job, I don't get mulligans," Stearns said. "I also recognize Pete had a tremendous year, and the totality of our production at first base wasn't good enough, and so now it's my job to ensure that we've got better success across our roster, but for the entire season, better production at first base as well."

The ever-analytical Stearns still doesn't seem to grasp that it wasn't strictly about production, but about what Alonso meant to the fanbase in an emotional capacity as well as the historic homers. But to be fair, if Polanco had hit 30 home runs and played plus-defense, the fans probably wouldn't have reacted the way they did to Alonso's return with the Baltimore Orioles .

Though Stearns played coy about pursuing free-agent ace Tarik Skubal , he was open about his intention to add starting pitching this winter. He has long believed free agency isn't the way to build a team, and he still does, saying the Mets will be selective in free agency.

An aggressive overhaul isn't the goal this winter, and there will be no fancy buzzwords.

"I think I'll retire the phrase run prevention," he joked. "I don't know that that one worked perfectly well."

The theme of the offseason seems to be making measured changes to help foster growth of the young core and maximize the talents of the veterans. Going into his fourth season leading the Mets, the pressure isn't lessening. Much like the team on the field, Stearns has to execute under the weight of those expectations.

articles.title: Bronny James adjusts to Lakers' life without LeBron: 'Feels like he's not here'
articles.summary: Bronny James has been focused on being a bigger part of the Lakers' rotation during the offseason with his father, LeBron James, now in Philadelphia.
articles.body:
Bronny James wanted to make it clear who came out on top the last time he played his father in golf.

"I won," James told reporters as he cracked a smile at Los Angeles Lakers media day on Monday, Sept. 28. "He's pretty pissed about this."

It was a quick, lighthearted moment that drew laughs from those in attendance, but it also helped address the elephant in the room: for the first time in his now three-year NBA career, Bronny won't be sharing a locker room with LeBron James .

"Feels like he's not here," James said matter of factly. "I don't really have an opinion on that. That's my dad, I spent 22 years, almost, with him. Just another experience that I'm gonna be a part of, and I'm excited to see how it's gonna feel during the season, too. Looking forward to it."

LeBron James takes center stage at 76ers media day

LeBron James left the Lakers for the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency this summer, marking an end to the first father-son duo to ever take the court together in an NBA game after two years as teammates. Bronny James spent much of that time in the G League, but he made a leap in year two last season and cracked the rotation in the Lakers' first-round playoff series against the Houston Rockets .

Now, with an almost entirely new cast of teammates centered around Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves , he sees room for even more growth as he sets off on his own path.

"It's just something that I've followed my entire life," James said. "You guys know me as Bronny, my real name is LeBron. I've been doing this for however long, so I think it's a motivating factor for me just getting up every day and trying to prove myself as Bronny instead of LeBron."

Bronny James has been focused on trying to be the most consistent version of himself over the offseason. The 21-year-old guard has been showing up every day to work on his dribbling, playmaking and "being relentless" on both ends of the court. He knows versatility is a priority in coach JJ Redick 's new scheme, and his best chance to get minutes is as a secondary ballhandler on offense and a point-of-attack defender when Dončić and Reaves are off the floor.

He's also gotten to know his new teammates pretty well, accompanying them on the team's trip to Slovenia. There, James told reporters, is where he felt the chemistry start to take off.

"We had some runs in practice, figuring out each other's game and just chilling off the court, getting to know each other," he said. "... I think that's going to carry over into the season pretty well."

Not only does this year's Lakers squad look different, they'll be playing differently than they did in JJ Redick's first two years as head coach. Redick has already mentioned he'll be switching up the defensive scheme to more man-on-man with newly acquired Walker Kessler parked near the paint to clean up anything that may come his way. Reaves and several other players also talked about a fast-paced free-flowing offense with less pick-and-roll.

"Everyone's young," James said. "... I feel like we can feed off each other's energy and there's gonna be a lot of guys that can go out, give full effort and turn up the game."

LeBron James, meanwhile, made it clear that he didn't make his free agency decision – possibly the last one of his 24-year NBA career – lightly, telling reporters in Philadelphia that "I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round . I know that for sure. Work needs to be done, and I'm ready to get to work."

While he got the blessing of the entire James family, Bronny said it wasn't cathartic moment by any means.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're gonna do and how we feel about each other," James said. "Wasn't really much, to be honest with you. He's got his own path and I've got my own. ... And he knows that I want to focus on that."

Those two paths are set to converge once more on Dec. 25, when the Lakers host the the 76ers at Crypto.com Arena in LeBron's return to Los Angeles .

"I'm excited to see him on Christmas," Bronny said.

articles.title: Prado Wins 2026 SMX Playoffs And $1 Million Prize
articles.summary: Spaniard holds off Deegan in tight final moto to claim the championship Photos by Align Media. Jorge Prado has won the 2026 Supermotocross World Championship...
articles.body:
Spaniard holds off Deegan in tight final moto to claim the championship

Jorge Prado has won the 2026 Supermotocross World Championship after beating Haiden Deegan by just 1.7s in the second moto of the Playoff Final at Thunder Ridge Nature Arena. The win, with triple points awarded for the final, gave Prado the nod in the final standings by a mere 7 points over Deegan. Prado becomes the first Spanish-born rider to win the SMX Playoffs and the $1 million winner's purse.

The Red Bull KTM rider did it the hard way, after a fifth-place finish in the first moto, while Deegan converted the holeshot into a wire-to-wire win by 3.1 seconds over Ken Roczen, with Hunter Lawrence third. Prado, who led the points standings heading into the Championship Final, started 10th but clawed his way to fifth. Deegan was tied for second behind Prado, and with triple points up for grabs, the win put him in a really good position heading into the final moto.

Prado answered with the holeshot in the second moto ahead of Deegan. The Monster Energy Star Racing Yamaha rider found the fastest laps of the moto in the second half, and reeled Prado in, drawing to within a bike length or two with roughly three and a half minutes remaining. Both riders had to deal with lapped riders, but Prado kept it clean enough to win by 1.731 seconds.

Deegan's 1-2 gave him the overall win and 75 points, bringing his championship total to 151 points. Prado's 5-1 results put him ahead of Lawrence's two third-place finishes, and giving him 66 points, enough to give him 158 on the season and 7 points ahead of Deegan for the SMX Championship.

"One year ago I wasn't even racing in the SMX post-season, but the Red Bull KTM Factory Racing team did an awesome job preparing me all winter long, every single week, and I also prepared myself the best I could to bounce back," Prado said. "That's what champions do, right?"

Prado will look to defend his SMX title next season, after signing a multi-year contract extension with Red Bull KTM Factory Racing. A two-time MXGP World Champion and two-time MX2 champion, Prado's next task will be to capture his first AMA title, either in Supercross or Pro Motocross.

articles.title: Illinois, Hauck part ways: ‘He felt it wasn’t working for him’
articles.summary: Bobby Hauck and Illinois parted ways just four games into the season.
articles.body:
Champaign, IL – It's now been over 24 hours since Illinois announced the departure of Defensive Coordinator Bobby Hauck.

Hauck was only four games into his stint in Champaign, after spending the better part of three decades at Montana.

The move came as a shock to many, including myself, and although there are many questions that need answering, Illini Head Coach Bret Bielema gave insight into the decision at Monday's press conference.

"Bobby reached out to me early Sunday morning and said he wanted to have a talk," Bielema said. "He felt it wasn't working for him."

It's a selfless move by Hauck, whose defense gave up 42 points to Ohio State on Saturday.

As much as it sucks to see Hauck leave almost as soon as he got to Illinois, the move was more than needed.

"I give Bobby a lot of credit for the full circle moment when he just said that I think your players deserve better than what's happening," Bielema said.

With multiple Illini defensive mishaps on Saturday, along with a subpar performance against Duke, the writing was on the wall – just maybe not this soon into the season.

Now the question turns to what direction this Illini defense takes.

"I have a conversation before the year starts with not only the play caller but the second guy that we'd go to," Bielema said.

As for who that second play caller is – that part is still a mystery.

There won't be another chance to possibly get insight on the defense this week either. As Bielema has tucked away his entire defense going into Purdue.

"I'm going to put the defense on lockdown this week," Bielema said. "No coach and no player is going to talk until Saturday after the game."

It's going to be a long week awaiting the Illini's Homecoming showdown against the Boilermakers. But we will undoubtedly learn what course the rest of the season will take on Saturday.

"Then Saturday you'll see the answer to what we put in place," Bielema said of his defense.

Regardless of what scheme or personal changes that come with Hauck's departure, the shock from the move, mixed with locker room chemistry, will be the hardest thing to handle going into the back half of the season.

"No one in the team room knew what was happening," Bielema said. "So I think it kind of caught everybody off guard."

Given the shock that the team must be facing, it makes complete sense for Bielema to take his defense out of the media spotlight this week.

However, the orange and blue now face a difficult challenge: have a short memory going into Saturday.

Despite the abrupt departure, Bielema didn't seem out of character on Monday. Bielema was his same jolly self, and even brushed off the fact that Hauck's exit could tank the 2026 season.

"I don't think it's going to be as big a deal from the outside world or from inside the building as you think," Bielema said. "Obviously the voice of gameday changes, but Bobby wasn't actually speaking the calls anyways."

Will the move not be a big deal? I'm cautiously optimistic; however, the Illini will answer that question along with a new defensive play caller this Saturday.

articles.title: Red Wings celebrate International League championship at ESL Ballpark
articles.summary: ROCHESTER, N.Y. (WROC) — The Rochester Red Wings celebrated their historic championship run with fans Monday night at ESL Ballpark. The Red Wings captured th...
articles.body:
ROCHESTER, N.Y. (WROC) — The Rochester Red Wings celebrated their historic championship run with fans Monday night at ESL Ballpark.

The Red Wings captured their first International League championship since 1997 last Thursday, defeating the Memphis Redbirds 3-2 to claim the title.

Rochester then advanced to the Triple-A National Championship Game on Saturday night, taking on the Oklahoma City Comets. The Wings fell just short of another title, losing 5-3 in extra innings.

But Monday night was all about celebrating the team's championship season and bringing the trophy home to Rochester.

Fans gathered at ESL Ballpark for a celebration featuring live music, food and drinks. Attendees also had the chance to take photos with the International League championship trophy and flag.

The title ended a nearly three-decade wait for the Red Wings, marking the franchise's first International League championship in 29 years.

articles.title: Built for October, Padres plan on World Series return after 28 years
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres and Chicago Cubs meet again in the NL wild-card round, but this time around the games will be at Petco Park.
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO — The last time the Chicago Cubs laid eyes on the San Diego Padres they had to refrain from laughing aloud in their faces.

And the Cubs humiliated the Padres , winning 23-3 , with No. 9 hitter Dansby Swanson hitting three home runs and driving in eight runs, handing the Padres their worst loss in the 58-year history of the franchise.

It was the Cubs' fifth consecutive victory, and the Padres' fifth consecutive loss, leaving the Padres' season on the brink.

Well, here they are meeting again, and, oh, how so much has changed.

The Padres these days just so happen to be the hottest team in baseball, winning 17 of their last 20 games, to not only storm into the postseason, but clinch the top wild-card spot, hosting the Cubs in the best-of-three wild-card series.

It's a rematch of the wild-card series a year ago, only this time the games will all be played at raucous Petco Park and not Wrigley Field.

The Padres (91-71) are in the postseason for the third consecutive year, fifth time in the last seven years, and believing this time around they could go where they have never gone before in franchise history.

World Series champions through the years

They've been to the big stage twice, back in 1984 when they knocked off the Cubs in the NLCS before losing in five games to the Detroit Tigers , and again in 1998 when they were swept by the New York Yankees .

The Padres might have a rotation held together by duct tape, but they have the nastiest bullpen in all of the land. No team can shorten games like the Padres with All-Star closer Mason Miller , setup man Adrian Morejon, and rookie Bradgley Rodriguez.

"We played them in a playoff series last year and understand how their bullpen is going to work and how they're going to use Miller and Morejon,'' Cubs manager Craig Counsell says, "and this year Bradgley Rodriguez has been added to that group as somebody who is pretty darn good.

"We've got to have good at-bats. We've got to make ourselves tough outs, and we're going to have to score against the bullpen, too, and we have scored against their bullpen. So I think we're confident.''

The Padres, who keep knocking on the playoff door without getting through, still are haunted by not putting away the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2024. They were up two games to one in the best-of-five division series, had Game 4 at home, and were shut out in the next two games. They lost in three games to the Cubs last year at Wrigley Field in the wild-card round.

But this time around, they truly believe their fate will be different.

"I think we're firing on all cylinders,'' says Padres ace Michael King , who will start Game 1 against Cubs starter Matthew Boyd . "I think the last two months, two and a half months, the offense has possibly been the best in baseball. We've really come together as a starting rotation, and the bullpen is obviously a strong piece.

"I think that, when you look at us, we don't really have many weaknesses. ... We're very confident in what we've been doing the last few weeks, and we're very happy that this is the time that we got hot, and we've just got to continue it throughout all this postseason.''

Padres star third baseman Manny Machado , who produced his lowest OPS (.711) in his career, batting just .217, still managed to hit 30 homers and drive in 91 runs. Fernando Tatis Jr. , who didn't homer until May 30, still hit .289 with 25 homers and 83 RBI. And they got huge production out of first baseman Ty France , signed to a minor-league contract this spring, who hit 21 homers with 72 RBI.

This is why Machado believes this version of the Padres is the best since his arrival in 2019, and could finally be the one that knocks off their mighty neighbors to the north, the Dodgers.

Machado might already have his sights set on the Dodgers. He asked a reporter on Monday, Sept. 28 why he was wearing a bright blue suit that resembled Dodger colors.

"Are you for San Diego,'' he asked the local reporter.

Machado: "Obviously not. I'm just asking.''

So why does Machado believe this team has its best chance to be playing in late October?

"I mean, experience,'' he said. "At the end of the day, it goes back to experience. We have a lot of the same group that was here last year. Hopefully we get a lot further. But ultimately, I think it's just believing in ourselves, believing in the group that we have in there and go out there and just continue to do what we've been doing.''

Even though the Cubs ended the Padres' season last year, and beat them up during the season by winning five of six games, Machado insists there will be no carry-over effect.

"It's a new year, it's a different year,'' Machado said. "Obviously, that stung last year for us. They played better ball than us last year. This year's going to be a little bit different.

"Playing in front of our home crowd and playing in front of these fans here, I think it's going to be a lot different. Definitely looking forward to that rematch for sure.''

The Padres enjoy one of the greatest home-field advantages in baseball, playing in front of fans that pack the joint nearly on a nightly basis. The Padres went a sizzling 26-6 in their last 32 home games this season.

"I think being at home is huge,'' Machado said. "We love playing here, playing in front of this crowd, playing in the stadium. Obviously sleeping at home and being at home is a big advantage, but I think the biggest one is playing in front of the home crowd. They've brought the energy all year. They're going to continue to do it.

"To have a postseason here at home in front of them, they're definitely going to bring the energy, and I think we all feed off of that.''

The Cubs realize what a difference it can make playing at home themselves at Wrigley Field, but instead of being intimidated, plan to embrace the hostility.

"They have a great atmosphere," Cubs second baseman Nico Hoerner told reporters in Tampa Bay on Sunday after their regular-season finale . "It's probably one of the places that's changed the most over the last 10 years or so. They have a great fan base. It'll be electric, a lot of fun and challenging."

The winner of the series will face the Milwaukee Brewers , who won an MLB-leading 103 games, and ended the Cubs' season a year ago.

This time around, the Padres want to be the ones to take a crack at the powerful Brewers, but first, they've got to get past the Cubs, who will have third Alex Bregman back in the lineup who suffered eight fractured bones in his face when hit by foul ball standing near the on-deck circle a week ago.

Bregman, who took a ground ball for the first time in a week on Monday, showed that he was ready with the bat Sunday when he went 4-for-4 with two homers.

"He's the man, to be honest,'' Cubs reliever Jacob Webb said. "That's tough to do. That's really cool and shows the kind of character that he has going through such a crazy injury. I mean, you're putting your career on the line at that point, but he's always prepared.

"He's a good dude. He knows what he's doing. He has his plan, and I think that's the biggest thing, is he wants to be here. He wants to win.''

No offense, the Padres say, but they would love to send Bregman home early, giving him all winter to heal.

"We're steady,'' King said. "We're confident. And we're going to go play Padres baseball.''

articles.title: O’Shea Jackson Jr. urges Lakers to keep Bronny James after personal admission
articles.summary: With LeBron James no longer on the Los Angeles Lakers, Bronny James faces a different kind of test. He remains with the team, but the question of what he can...
articles.body:
With LeBron James no longer on the Los Angeles Lakers , Bronny James faces a different kind of test. He remains with the team, but the question of what he can build without his father beside him now sits squarely in front of him. O'Shea Jackson Jr. already knows where he stands.

"Keep him @Lakers," Jackson wrote on X in response to a post sharing Bronny's comments about forging his own identity.

Bronny spoke to Spectrum SportsNet at Lakers Media Day about playing without his father. He sounded eager to find out what changes, including how people around the team interact with him.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'm excited for the experience, to experience something different, him not being here," Bronny said. "[Excited] to see how the staff treats me without him being there, and all my teammates and stuff like that."

Bronny James wants to prove himself on his own terms

In the post Jackson shared, Bronny put the distinction between his name and his identity more plainly. "You guys know me as Bronny, my real name is LeBron," he said. "I've been doing this for however long so I think it's a motivating factor for me just getting up every day and trying to prove myself as Bronny instead of LeBron."

That ambition has followed him since the Lakers selected him with the 55th pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. The selection drew scrutiny that most players chosen so late would never encounter. His father's departure does not erase that debate, but it gives Bronny a chance to answer it through his own work.

Jackson's message was brief. In two words, though, he made clear that he wants the Lakers to give Bronny that chance in Los Angeles .

articles.title: Hurts’ return sparks Eagles before halftime: 10 takeaways vs. Bears
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts returned from a concussion evaluation and scored before halftime, pulling the Eagles within 10-7 of the Bears
articles.body:
In what was a first 30 minutes that we couldn't have imagined, Jalen Hurts' concussion evaluation became the defining moment of a first half the Eagles nearly let slip away Monday night in Chicago. While Hurts was in the medical tent after a hit by D'Marco Jackson, Andy Dalton entered and threw an interception in the end zone to end a 95-yard drive. Hurts was cleared to return, completed four straight passes and scored on a sneak just before halftime, cutting the Bears ' lead to 10-7.

After an uneven first and second quarter, Philadelphia stayed close despite Dalton's interception, a lost Tank Bigsby fumble and five penalties. Saquon Barkley provided the offense's most consistent production, totaling 73 yards on 11 carries behind a reshuffled line, while Quinyon Mitchell's fourth-down pass breakup kept Chicago from turning Bigsby's fumble into points. The Eagles still have work to do against Case Keenum, who threw for 149 yards and a touchdown in the half.

With the second half set to begin, here are ten first-half takeaways from Soldier Field in Chicago.

1. Jalen Hurts' evaluation changed the half. Hurts went to the medical tent after a hit by D'Marco Jackson. Following an intense evaluation for a concussion and cleared to return. He finished the half 10-of-13 for 111 yards and added a rushing touchdown.

2. The backup's one snap was costly. Andy Dalton entered while Hurts was being evaluated and threw an interception to Dillon Thieneman in the end zone. Philadelphia had driven 95 yards before the turnover ended its best scoring opportunity so far.

3. Hurts answered immediately. After returning, Hurts completed four straight passes and led an eight-play, 67-yard touchdown drive in 1:52. His sneak on a snap just before the clock expired cut Chicago's lead to 10-7.

4. Saquon Barkley looks like the centerpiece again. Barkley rushed for 73 yards on 11 carries, averaging 6.6 yards per attempt. He repeatedly reached the second level and gave Philadelphia the consistent ground production it had been seeking.

5. The reshuffled offensive line is moving people. Drew Kendall drew attention for his work against Grady Jarrett, and the Eagles created room for Barkley. The protection also held up: Philadelphia allowed no first-half sack.

6. Turnovers have erased promising work. Tank Bigsby fumbled, giving Chicago the ball at the Eagles' 15. Dalton's interception ended the 95-yard drive. Philadelphia is within three points despite losing both first-half turnovers.

7. The penalties keep putting the offense in trouble. Tyler Steen's holding call preceded Bigsby's fumble, while an intentional grounding call stalled an earlier possession. The Eagles had five penalties in the half, leaving points and field position on the table.

8. Case Keenum has found a rhythm. With Caleb Williams out, Keenum completed 15 of 21 passes for 149 yards and a touchdown. Luther Burden III led the way with five catches for 59 yards, including an 8-yard score on Chicago's opening drive.

9. Quinyon Mitchell kept the deficit manageable. After Bigsby's fumble, the Bears reached scoring range but came away empty. Mitchell's fourth-down pass breakup completed a stand that prevented Chicago from stretching its 7-0 lead.

10. The safety rotation is worth watching. Marcus Epps missed two tackles on the opening touchdown drive, according to Jeff McLane. Michael Carter II replaced him for part of the next series, but Epps returned later. Vic Fangio appears to be rotating the two as the defense works to settle down.

articles.title: What Suns' Mat Ishbia, Devin Booker think about Miles Bridges trade
articles.summary: The Phoenix Suns open the 2026-27 regular season on Oct. 21 at the Portland Trail Blazers. Offseason moves were a hot topic at media day.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns team owner Mat Ishbia and franchise all-time leading scorer Devin Booker addressed several topics during the team's media day Sept. 28 at Mortgage Matchup Center, with one being the Miles Bridges trade.

Phoenix moved Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and an unprotected 2033 first-round pick to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick.

"I feel great about the Miles Bridges trade first. First off, Royce and Grayson were two great players, great part of our team," Ishbia said. "We're gonna definitely miss those two guys, but bringing in Miles, on the court, he's a phenomenal player. He's done amazing things. He's gonna be a great fit from a cultural perspective. His work ethic, his drive, his athleticism, his toughness. It fits exactly what we're building here in Phoenix. And so, from a basketball perspective, we feel extremely great about that fit on our team, and he was a player that we targeted as that."

Bridges averaged 17.1 points on 46% shooting, 5.8 rebounds and 3.2 assists in 2025-26 in 77 games. The 6-7, 225-pound forward brings experience, athleticism and physicality to the power forward position.

"He's something that we were lacking a bit last year with his size, his versatility on both ends of the court," Booker said. "I think he's an underrated playmaker from his position. Somebody that can get the rebound and push the break also and he can exploit matchups that aren't his size. So he can take advantage of the mismatches. I'm excited to share the court with him."

Behind the scenes of Phoenix Suns' 2026 Media Day

Bridges was involved in a domestic violence incident with the mother of his children, for which the NBA imposed a 30-game suspension without pay in April 2023. He missed the entire 2022-23 season. In recognition of that outcome, the NBA deemed 20 games of the suspension had been served.

"Off the court, what Miles did was unacceptable, cannot be condoned by anyone in America, hopefully," Ishbia said. "You know, that's just completely off. Now, he's been held accountable. He showed remorse, you know, and we have standards here in Phoenix, and that's not to our standards, and it will not be allowed anywhere near that type of level here in Phoenix."

Bridges played college basketball at Michigan State, where Ishbia was part of the 2000 national championship team.

"I feel extremely good about Miles and how he feels about what happened and how he's gonna be a better man,' Ishbia said. "And he has taken accountability. And so Miles got a second chance in Charlotte, and now he's here in Phoenix. And I think his job every day is to show on the court what an amazing player he is, and then also off the court, to show everyone what kind of guy he can be in this community, with his kids, with his family, and all the things he can do around the community. I'm really confident and excited for you guys to meet Miles and see Miles in that way. And so we feel really good about it."

Ishbia also addressed the Suns yielding an unprotected first-round pick for Bridges.

"I've heard for years that I don't have any draft picks," Ishbia said. "We've had a first-round pick each of the last three years. We got them each of the next four years. (Suns general manager) Brian Gregory and his scouting team, the whole team, these guys do a hell of a job getting good young talent. I'm not going to name every player, but from (Khaman Maluach, Rasheer Fleming, Koa Peat). Of course, Ryan (Dunn) and Oso (Ighodaro). We've got great young players, and we got picks.

"So I'm not worried about the 2033 first-round pick. We also got a first-round pick back. We got a second-round pick back. We feel really good about our ability to build around this team, but we got a great player with that pick, and also giving up a couple other good players, and we feel really good that our team is better this year going into it than we were last year, and Miles is a big part of that."

In the final year of a three-year, $75-million deal, Bridges is eligible for a three-year extension up to $86 million.

articles.title: This overlooked player will make or break Phillies' chances vs. Braves in NL WC
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies spent the final week of the regular season trying to avoid a collapse. They secured a playoff spot with a win on Sunday, but their...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies spent the final week of the regular season trying to avoid a collapse. They secured a playoff spot with a win on Sunday, but their reward is a trip to Atlanta for a best-of-three Wild Card Series against the Braves. If Philadelphia hopes to extend its season, its biggest stars cannot be the only hitters who show up.

Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper will command attention . Trea Turner will have chances to set the table. Alec Bohm and Brandon Marsh have had solid seasons. Bryson Stott , though, might be the player who determines whether the Phillies can turn those opportunities into enough runs to beat Atlanta.

Luis Arraez has been ruled out of the Wild Card series with his left-ankle injury. Stott is back at second base in the meantime.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Stott finished the regular season batting .256 with a .735 OPS, 10 home runs, 67 RBIs and 27 stolen bases. Those numbers will not make him the headline name in this series. His value is in how many ways he can affect a close game: reaching base, taking an extra base, and making a difficult play at second. Philadelphia may need all three against a Braves team that won 94 games.

Bryson Stott is finding his swing as the Phillies need it most

The Phillies' offense struggled badly in September, ranking near the bottom of the majors in batting average, OPS and runs per game. Stott had his own slump during the month, but he finished differently. Over his final seven games, he went 9-for-23, drew six walks and posted a .517 on-base percentage. He's hitting .320 over his last 15 games as well.

Stott saved one of his best performances for the game Philadelphia had to win. He collected three hits against the Rays on Sunday, including an RBI double, and stole a base as the Phillies clinched. One strong game does not guarantee a productive playoff series, but it gives Philadelphia a timely reminder of what its second baseman can do when he is comfortable at the plate.

Stott does not need to hit a home run off Chris Sale in Game 1 to matter. A long at-bat against Atlanta's ace could push up his pitch count. A walk or single could give the next hitter a chance with a runner in scoring position. In a three-game series, those smaller contributions can be the difference between making Sale work and allowing him to cruise.

That challenge begins immediately. Sale posted a 2.16 ERA this season and a 2.08 ERA in four starts against the Phillies. He is capable of shutting down any lineup, especially one that has spent much of September searching for answers. If Stott can help create traffic against him, Philadelphia gives its bigger bats something to work with.

Stott's glove carries extra weight in Atlanta

Stott's defense gives Philadelphia a dependable presence. That matters in a series likely to feature tight games.

A clean double play behind Philadelphia's pitchers could stop an Atlanta rally before it grows. A ball Stott reaches in the gap might keep Ronald Acuña Jr. or Matt Olson from coming up with a runner already in scoring position. Those plays rarely get the same attention as a home run, but the Phillies cannot afford to give the Braves more chances.

Philadelphia has beaten Atlanta in each of their past three postseason meetings, including Division Series victories in 2022 and 2023. That history will add to the atmosphere at Truist Park, but it will not score any runs this week. The current Phillies must find a way to support their pitching and string together better at-bats than they managed for much of September.

Stott is positioned to help them do both. If he keeps reaching base, uses his speed, and makes the plays expected of him at second, Philadelphia has a better chance to send its stars to the plate with something on the line. If his late offensive surge fades and the Phillies continue to waste outs, their stay in October could be brief. That makes Stott an overlooked X-factor in a series where every opportunity will count.

articles.title: History, drama & change - How Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity helped Super League Grand Final enter a new era
articles.summary: The 2026 Super League Grand Final marks the first time that none of St Helens, Leeds Rhinos, or Wigan Warriors have been involved; watch Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity in the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports from 5pm
articles.body:
It has been pondered for a while if the playing field was starting to level, if these teams that once could not touch the big boys, now had the funds, the backing, the know-how to reach the top.

Not only that, would they leave the original 'Super League giants' in shock that others have not only caught up, but have started to usurp them.

To understand the significance you have to know the context. This is the first Grand Final EVER that does not include one of St Helens, Leeds Rhinos, or Wigan Warriors. It has taken until the 29th staging of this event for one of those teams to not be involved.

You only have to look at the list of winners to see it has been complete and utter domination by those three, with a sprinkling of Bradford and last year's historic win by Hull KR.

St Helens have won it on nine occasions, Leeds eight times, Wigan have seven Grand Final wins, and Bradford three. Hull KR have a '1' next to their name - that is what one of Wakefield Trinity and Warrington Wolves will have come Saturday night.

In 2026, St Helens missed out on the play-offs for the first time in their history, Leeds were beaten by Warrington, Wigan were dominated by Wakefield, Bradford finished bottom, and Hull KR were dumped out by the Wolves in the Eliminators.

The guard has started to change. History alone is no longer enough to power you through and now, there are sides intent on creating their own lasting legacy that will do everything in their power to make it happen.

When Warrington and Wakefield walk out to the cacophony of noise at Old Trafford on Saturday, that exact history beckons.

They say that the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different outcome. Wakefield and Warrington have ripped up repetition and instead decided that making waves is the way forward.

Indeed, it is a final in which we cannot look at either team as the one that has 'been there, done it, and got the t-shirt'.

Nerves will be on display but in the best way because they highlight once again that sport and fairytales intertwine - they will be a sign of a great story, an exceptional story, and it is up to one of Warrington and Wakefield to be the protagonist.

The Wakey way: From relegation to jubilation

Wakefield have provided an underdog story for the ages - the team were relegated in 2024 and within two years of returning to Super League, they are in the biggest match of them all.

Not many would have believed that could occur except those in their inner sanctum. That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

They have turned potential that was nearly forgotten into diamonds on the cusp of international selection. They have built an environment players want to be involved in, and now, they are 80 minutes from one of the biggest moments in the city's history.

Mills actually started his career at Warrington and worked up to being one of the best brains in recruitment. When Powell left Warrington, so did he and now, they have created their own unique and special blend of experience and raw talent that has impressed throughout 2026.

'It is always your year': The moment the chant ends?

Warrington also have their chance to live down a chant that has followed them and get their reward for trusting the process.

Opposition fans have forever sang 'It is always your year' at the Wolves faithful, taunting them with their lack of Super League silverware. They have had the backing for a long time, have been near the top, have Challenge Cups, but despite appearing at the Grand Final four times previously, have never gotten over the line.

It has taken eight years for Warrington to rebuild to this point and get to the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again. They finished outside the play-offs in 2025 but came together, backed their coach, worked on their culture, and became arguably the best 'team' in the league.

If you play even slightly poorly they will pounce and don't expect points against them to come easily. They back their youth to shine and they have. They want to work hard for each other and will leave it all out there.

They will now want to be able to say 'Just like the last one, it is always our year' and mean it.

It is also a huge night for their captain George Williams. Williams made a massive call back in 2021 to not return to his hometown club of Wigan and head to Warrington on his return from the NRL.

It has been levelled against him the amount Wigan have achieved in those five years but a vindication could be on the horizon if he shines in his last Warrington hoorah.

Two teams will step out onto the Old Trafford turf with a million reasons running around their minds of why this is their moment and those odd doubtful thoughts telling them the alternative.

After 80 minutes, we will know which team has defined themselves as the flashpoint of the potential beginning of a new era.

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

articles.summary: Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White gets blamed for the team’s terrible Game 1 loss. The Indiana Fever had a far-from-ideal start to the 2026 WNBA playo...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White gets blamed for the team's terrible Game 1 loss.

The Indiana Fever had a far-from-ideal start to the 2026 WNBA playoffs as they were blown out by the Las Vegas Aces in a 102-85 Game 1 defeat.

As a result, the Fever are facing early elimination ahead of Game 2. But what went wrong for the Fever in the playoff opener?

Well, according to WNBA analyst Rachel DeMita, head coach Stephanie White's poor mentality was to blame for the terrible loss.

Rachel DeMita sounds alarm bells over Stephanie White's poor mentality

While the Fever still have a chance to make a comeback in Game 2 and extend the series, DeMita's analysis of White's coaching hints that the probability is pretty low.

"I was seeing in the postgame press conference and the pregame press conference from yesterday's Indiana Fever versus Las Vegas Aces game that were truly, truly alarming.

"And it's one of the biggest reasons that I just don't think the Indiana Fever have what it takes this year in these playoffs to win anything," DeMita said on her podcast.

She added, ""I don't see them making it out of the first round, and it starts with the mentality, and it starts with the mentality of coach Stephanie White…

"It's disappointing to see because I've definitely held my tongue, bit my tongue, you know, coming down really hard on the coaching staff because, firstly, I don't really like trashing anyone."

The Fever's poor form towards the tail end of the season, combined with a potential first-round postseason exit, will only spell trouble for White.

After all, Fever fans have already been demanding her firing, and a first-round exit with arguably the best offense in the league is indeed a terrible look for the head coach.

articles.body:
We asked you to send in your questions for football reporter Nick Mashiter to answer. In the first of a two-part Q&A on Tuesday, he addresses Aston Villa's recruitment and lack of success with wide attacking players.

Prit asked: Does having a slow start two years in a row mean Villa need to review their transfer strategy and ensure all business is conducted at least one week before the season starts?

Nick: The summer's transfer business, for a lot of clubs, was always going to be towards the end of the window because of the World Cup.

It was natural things were going to concertina up and, as a result, Villa's business - like many - was mostly done in August.

In an ideal world, every club and manager would like to do it earlier and Unai Emery has made it clear he wants the transfer window shut before the start of the season.

He has said Villa are essentially still in pre-season while the new players settle, which has contributed to the slow start to the campaign.

Last summer's business was limited anyway - Harvey Elliott , Jadon Sancho and Victor Lindelof arriving on deadline day. Like every club, Villa will plan - but then still have to react to the market.

Alex asked: Why do we keep bringing in wide attacking players that turn out to be not for us - for example, Nicolo Zaniolo , Elliott, Sancho and Alejandro Garnacho ? Don't we do our due diligence?

Nick: The jury will remain out on Garnacho for a bit longer, but the early signs are not positive, with the winger left on the bench for the past four games.

But we need to look across the board, not just at the wide players.

How many signings can be called a complete success under Emery? Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans are in an exclusive club.

Pau Torres and Ian Maatsen may join them, but even Amadou Onana struggles to make the list given his injury record. Lindelof has done a job, as has Marco Bizot when called on.

Evann Guessand , Andres Garcia, Enzo Barrenechea , Samuel Iling-Junior , Jaden Philogene , Moussa Diaby and Lewis Dobbin all came and went without making much - if any, in some cases - impact.

Jhon Duran and Donyell Malen created their own headlines but were either not consistent enough - not something which can be levelled at Malen with Roma now - or never earned Emery's full faith.

Come back to this page later on Tuesday for part two of the Q&A, which will focus on Emery and whether Villa have adequately replaced the players who left in the summer.

articles.title: Brennan Poole's race recap in the Truck Chase race at Kansas in 2026
articles.summary: Check out Brennan Poole's race recap in the NASCAR Truck Series Chase race at Kansas Speedway during the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Brennan Poole finished 17th at Kansas Speedway in Spire Motorsports' No. 7 Chevrolet. Poole started 19th and remained around the middle of the field for most of Saturday's weather-interrupted race.

The veteran stayed clear of the major Stage 3 crash and avoided the flat tires that affected several competitors during the closing run. Poole gained two positions and finished on the lead lap, 9.619 seconds behind race winner Kaden Honeycutt. His truck remained intact throughout a race that lasted deep into the evening because of the lengthy weather stoppage.

Poole received zero Truck Series driver points because he was designated as ineligible for championship points at Kansas. His 17th-place finish therefore did not alter the Truck driver standings or Chase picture. The result still contributed to the No. 7 team's owner points and provided Spire with a completed race despite Poole's ineligible driver status.
